AI.description: Title of the AI picker dialog on the war setup screen (gw_start), and the label of the button in the co-op setup strip that opens it, beside "Commander" and "Game Options". (unit_names.js:26, exiles.js:448)

"Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Anti-Nuke Launcher"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Anti-Nuke Launcher Upgrade Tech halves the cost of SR-24 Shield Missile Defense missiles."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_antinuke.js)

Anti-Nuke Launcher Upgrade Tech halves t.message: Anti-Nuke Launcher Upgrade Tech halves the cost of SR-24 Shield Missile Defense missiles.

Must match the opening words of its description. (gwaio_anti_orbital.js:10)

Artemis Upgrade Tech allows targeting of.message: Artemis Upgrade Tech allows targeting of planetary units by the railgun platform.

Artillery.description: Penchant name: a one-word style bias an AI Commander can be given when the war's AI is set to PENCHANT. On the galaxy map it is appended after the personality trait in the "Personality:" row, joined with a space (e.g. "Aggressive Artillery"), so it must read as a noun/adjective that can follow a trait word; word order of that pairing cannot be changed. Singular, no punctuation. "Artillery" = favours long-range artillery units. (ai.js:149)

Artillery Ammunition Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. This card raises the damage of all artillery structures by 25% and cuts their ammunition cost by 90%. 'Tech' is the game's own term for a Galactic War technology; a short noun-phrase title, not a sentence. Must match the opening words of its description. (gwc_damage_artillery.js:11)

Artillery Ammunition Tech increases the.message: Artillery Ammunition Tech increases the damage of all artillery structures by 25% and reduces their ammunition cost by 90%. Requires technology to build artillery structures and units.
Artillery Ammunition Tech increases the.description: Card description, shown in the card tooltip in the Data Bank and when the card is dealt. Effect: damage of artillery structure shells x1.25 and their energy ammunition demand x0.1. The last sentence warns that the card is only dealt once the player already has the 'Artillery Tech' card. Keep '25%' and '90%'; opening words must be identical to the card name 'Artillery Ammunition Tech'. (gwc_damage_artillery.js:9)

Artillery Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown in the loadout picker when starting a war, in the Data Bank and its tooltip; the same string is also shown as the hint on the greyed-out (locked) version of the card. This loadout starts the player with all artillery structures at 25% cost and lets the Commander build radar, the double-barrelled laser turret and basic artillery. Noun phrase used as a title. Must agree with the opening words of its description 'The Artillery Commander loadout contains...'. (gwc_start_artillery.js:42, 49)

Artillery Fabrication Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. Artillery Fabrication Tech reduces metal.description: Card description, shown in the card tooltip in the Data Bank and when the card is dealt. Artillery Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. This card unlocks artillery structures for building. (gwc_enable_artillery.js:10)

As Osiris replaced pieces of himself wit.message: As Osiris replaced pieces of himself with those of fallen foes, he would store older parts for replacements and repairs. Eventually, Osiris acquired enough spare parts to construct an entirely new commander. This would be the birth of the first Seeker.
As Osiris replaced pieces of himself wit.description: Lore paragraph for the Revenants faction, one of five shown at random as the description of a Revenants-held system in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map. Stock flavour text: Osiris is a commander name, Seeker a faction term; keep the final full stop. (gw_faction_3.js:137)

BASIC FABBERS:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a dropdown of numbers and means the maximum number of basic fabbers (T1 builder units) the AI may have per army; tooltip: "Maximum number of basic fabbers per army." Noun phrase, plural, upper-case; keep the trailing colon. Sibling: "ADVANCED FABBERS:". (ai_settings.html:147)

BASIC: base game tech cards.description:
One line of the tooltip beside the tech-card deck dropdown on the war setup screen (gw_start). Lines read "DECK NAME: what it contains", joined with
by the code; third-party decks append their own lines in the same shape. BASIC is the base game's card deck and GALACTIC WAR OVERHAUL is this mod's; keep the mod name as the game's own translation of "Galactic War Overhaul" renders it, uppercased. Keep the colon; no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoCardsTooltip)

BEGINNER: you completed the tutorial.description:
One line of the difficulty tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start): the "?" beside the Difficulty dropdown lists every difficulty level, one per line, as "LEVEL: who it suits". The upper-case word before the colon is the difficulty level's name as it appears in the dropdown; keep it as the game's own translation of that level renders it (uppercased) and keep the colon. The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) BEGINNER is the easiest level.

BOUNTIES: earn an economic multiplier fo.message: BOUNTIES: earn an economic multiplier for every kill.
BOUNTIES: earn an economic multiplier fo.description:
One line of the Game Modifiers tooltip on the galaxy map's system intelligence panel (gw_play). Each line is "MODIFIER NAME: what it does", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is a game modifier that must match the same modifier's name elsewhere (the Game Modifiers list and the in-battle win-conditions line use the title-case form: Bounties, Land Anywhere, Sudden Death, Eradicate). Keep the colon and the full stop; no line break in the string. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js, gwoGameModifiersTooltip)

BRONZE: you beat vanilla Galactic War.message: BRONZE: you beat vanilla Galactic War
BRONZE: you beat vanilla Galactic War.description:

The upper-case word before the colon is the difficulty level's name as it appears in the dropdown; keep it as the game's own translation of that level renders it (uppercased) and keep the colon. The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) "Vanilla" means the unmodded base game; Galactic War is the game mode name, use its stock translation.

Backpacker Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown in the loadout picker when starting a war, in the Data Bank and its tooltip; the same string is also shown as the hint on the greyed-out (locked) version of the card. This loadout gives 12 extra Data Bank card slots (16 in total) but starts with only a bot fabricator, a bot factory and the Dox. 'Backpacker' suggests travelling light; a noun-phrase title. Must agree with its description 'Contains 16 data banks. Alas, travelling light...'. (gwaio_start_backpacker.js:19, 26)

Name of the built-in tech-card deck containing only the base game's cards, shown in the deck picker on the war setup screen (gw_start) and in the "Deck:" row of the war-info panel. Basic Manufacturing - This modified vers.message: Basic Manufacturing - This modified version of the Metal Extractor can be placed anywhere, but costs more and produces at a decreased rate. Cannot stack with the Advanced Metal Extractor. Produces metal.
Basic Manufacturing - This modified vers.description: In-game unit description that replaces the stock Metal Extractor description in the build bar tooltip when the 'Planetary Excavation Commander' loadout is in use. With that loadout the extractor no longer needs a metal spot, costs 150% and produces 50%; it cannot be built on top of an Advanced Metal Extractor. 'Basic Manufacturing - ' is a heading prefix; keep the hyphen separator and the final short sentence 'Produces metal.' as in stock unit descriptions. Keep 'Metal Extractor' and 'Advanced Metal Extractor' as the stock unit names; this text pairs with the sibling 'Advanced Manufacturing - ...' string. (nem_start_planetary.js:33)

Basic Vehicle Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. This card unlocks the basic Vehicle Factory and basic vehicles. 'Tech' is the game's own term for a Galactic War technology; a short noun-phrase title, not a sentence. Must agree with its description, which begins 'Basic Vehicle tech enables building...'. (gwc_enable_vehicles_t1.js:11)

Basic Vehicle tech enables building of b.message: Basic Vehicle tech enables building of basic vehicle and basic vehicle factories. Basic vehicle factories are built via your commander or any basic fabricator.
Basic Vehicle tech enables building of b.description: Card description, shown in the card tooltip in the Data Bank and when the card is dealt. Effect: adds the basic Vehicle Factory and every basic vehicle to the player's build list. 'Basic Vehicle tech' refers to the card name 'Basic Vehicle Tech'; 'basic vehicle' in the source is a typo for the plural 'basic vehicles', translate as plural. 'Commander' and 'fabricator' are the game's own terms. (gwc_enable_vehicles_t1.js:9)

Basic air tech enables building of mobil.message: Basic air tech enables building of mobile air units and factories. Basic air factories are built via your commander or any basic fabricator.
Basic air tech enables building of mobil.description: Card description, shown in the card tooltip in the Data Bank and when the card is dealt. Effect: adds the basic Air Factory and every basic mobile air unit to the player's build list. 'Basic air tech' refers to the card name 'Basic Air Tech'; the source uses lower case here, but keep the same words. 'Commander' and 'fabricator' are the game's own terms. (gwc_enable_air_t1.js:9)

Beginner.description:
Difficulty tier name for a Galactic War. Shown as the selected tier on the war setup screen (gw_start), in the "Difficulty:" row of the war-info panel on the galaxy map, in the co-op lobby title ("GWO Co-op - Difficulty: X"), and as the first part of the auto-generated war name (" - Players - - "). Noun, singular, title case, no punctuation. Must agree with the upper-cased tier name used in the difficulty tooltip ("BEGINNER: you completed the tutorial
CASUAL: ..."). The ten tiers are Beginner, Casual, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Uber, Custom. Beginner is the easiest tier and is also the fallback used when an old save records no difficulty. (difficulty_levels.js:4, ai.js:381)

Bigger galaxies will result in more comm.message: Bigger galaxies will result in more commanders, larger maps, higher CPU and RAM requirements, and will likely pose a greater challenge to complete.
Bigger galaxies will result in more comm.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the galaxy size picker on the war setup screen (gw_start). Full sentence; keep the full stop; CPU and RAM stay as-is. (size_tooltip.html:3)

Bionic Augmentation Commander Of Neutral.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown in the loadout picker when starting a war, in the Data Bank and its tooltip; the same string is also shown as the hint on the greyed-out (locked) version of the card. The name is a deliberate backronym spelling 'BACON'; it is a joke title, so a translation may keep the English or invent an equivalent playful expansion. The loadout costs 3 Data Bank slots but gives the Commander double fire rate, triple health, five times speed and a cheaper Uber Cannon. Must agree with the opening words of its description 'The Bionic Augmentation Commander Of Neutralizing loadout contains...'. (gwc_start_combatcdr.js:35, 43)

Bluehawk Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_bluehawk, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Bluehawk" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Bluehawk Upgrade Tech doubles the number of tactical missiles Bluehawks fire per volley."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_bluehawk.js)

Bluehawk Upgrade Tech doubles the number.message: Bluehawk Upgrade Tech doubles the number of tactical missiles Bluehawks fire per volley.
Bluehawk Upgrade Tech doubles the number.description: Card description, shown in the card tooltip in the Data Bank and when the card is dealt. Effect: the Bluehawk gets duplicate surface and anti-orbital missile launchers on its second muzzle, so each volley has twice the missiles. 'Bluehawks' is the plural of the unit name; keep the proper noun. Opening words must be identical to the card name 'Bluehawk Upgrade Tech'. The game appends the separate string 'Adds a new slot for another technology.' after this text, so do not add that idea here. (gwaio_upgrade_bluehawk.js:8)

Boom Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_boom, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Boom" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Boom Upgrade Tech replaces Dox with Booms in the Lob. Enables the building of Lobs."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_boom.js)

Boom Upgrade Tech replaces Dox with Boom.message: Boom Upgrade Tech replaces Dox with Booms in the Lob. Enables the building of Lobs.
Boom Upgrade Tech replaces Dox with Boom.description: Card description, shown in the card tooltip in the Data Bank and when the card is dealt. Effect: the Lob (a structure that launches bots across the map) is added to the player's build list, and the unit it launches changes from the Dox (basic bot) to the Boom (suicide bot). Keep 'Dox', 'Boom(s)' and 'Lob(s)' as proper-noun unit names; note 'Dox' is used unchanged in the plural while 'Booms' and 'Lobs' take a plural, so adapt to the target language's convention. Opening words must be identical to the card name 'Boom Upgrade Tech'. The game appends the separate string 'Adds a new slot for another technology.' after this text, so do not add that idea here. (gwaio_upgrade_boom.js:8)

Boomer.description: Bugs unit display name, shown in unit lists, card tooltips and the Which Units? panel. A small suicide bug (bug_boomer), a land unit that explodes on contact. The name is a proper noun: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean the way the game's own unit tables do. The same string is also the display name of the "Boomer" AI personality in shared/ai.js:177 (an AI that favours suicide bots), so one translation serves both uses. (bugs.js:447)

Boss.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel of the galaxy map (gw_play) and in the war-info panel. Adjective or noun used as a label, singular, no punctuation. A penchant word (Artillery, Fortress, Assault...) may be appended after it with a space, so keep it short. The same trait key is shared by all four stock factions and the Cluster faction; translate it once. "Boss" is the personality of each faction's final boss commander (e.g. Metrarch the Machinist); noun. (gw_faction_0.js:21 and the other faction files, cluster_faction.js:22)

Boss Commanders.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a number dropdown (how many Commanders make up the faction boss's army); tooltip: "Number of Commanders in the boss's army." Written in title case to match an existing translation entry and up-cased by CSS on screen; keep title case, no trailing punctuation (the colon is outside the tag). Noun phrase, plural. (ai_settings.html:62)

Bot Ammunition Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. This card raises the damage of all bots by 25%. 'Tech' is the game's own term for a Galactic War technology; a short noun-phrase title, not a sentence. Must match the opening words of the description 'Bot Ammunition Tech increases damage...'. (gwc_damage_bots.js:10)

Bot Ammunition Tech increases damage of.message: Bot Ammunition Tech increases damage of all bots by 25%
Bot Ammunition Tech increases damage of.description: Card description, shown in the card tooltip in the Data Bank and when the card is dealt. Effect: damage of every bot's weapon x1.25. 'Bots' is the game's land-unit class; reuse its stock translation. Keep '25%'; the source has no final full stop. Opening words must be identical to the card name 'Bot Ammunition Tech'. (gwc_damage_bots.js:8)

Bot Armor Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. This card raises the health of all bots by 50%. 'Tech' is the game's own term for a Galactic War technology; a short noun-phrase title, not a sentence. Must match the opening words of the description 'Bot Armor Tech increases health...'. (gwc_health_bots.js:10)

Bot Armor Tech increases health of all b.message: Bot Armor Tech increases health of all bots by 50%
Bot Armor Tech increases health of all b.description: Card description, shown in the card tooltip in the Data Bank and when the card is dealt. Effect: health of every bot x1.5. Keep '50%'; the source has no final full stop. Opening words must be identical to the card name 'Bot Armor Tech'. (gwc_health_bots.js:8)

Bot Combat Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. This card gives all bots +50% health, +25% damage and +50% speed. 'Tech' is the game's own term for a Galactic War technology; a short noun-phrase title, not a sentence. Must match the opening words of the description 'Bot Combat Tech increases health of all bots...'. (gwc_combat_bots.js:11)

Bot Combat Tech increases health of all.message: Bot Combat Tech increases health of all bots by 50%, damage by 25%, and speed by 50%
Bot Combat Tech increases health of all.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bot Combat Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card multiplies max health and movement speed of every mobile bot by 1.5 and the damage of bot weapons by 1.25. Keep 50%, 25% and 50% exactly. 'Bot' here is the unit class (bipedal walkers built at a Bot Factory), not a robot in general; use the game's own term for Bot. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Combat Tech'. There is no full stop at the end in English. (gwc_combat_bots.js:9)

Bot Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started and afterwards as the first card in the Data Bank list on the galaxy map. This loadout gives the player the basic bot factory and basic bots at the start of the war. Noun phrase, a title: 'Commander' is the player's commander unit, 'Bot' is the unit class it favours. Follow the pattern used by the other '<X> Commander' loadout names so they read as one series. Must agree with the card text 'The Bot Commander loadout contains basic bot factories.' (gwc_start_bot.js:18)

Bot Cooldown Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card halves the cooldown time between builds for every bot factory (basic and advanced). Short title, noun phrase; 'Cooldown' is the factory's pause between finishing one unit and starting the next. Keep the game's own term for Tech and Bot. Must match the wording used at the start of its description 'Bot Cooldown Tech halves the cooldown time...'. (gwaio_cooldown_bots.js:10)

Bot Cooldown Tech halves the cooldown ti.message: Bot Cooldown Tech halves the cooldown time between builds for all bot factories.
Bot Cooldown Tech halves the cooldown ti.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bot Cooldown Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies factory_cooldown_time of every bot factory by 0.5, so a bot factory starts its next unit twice as quickly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Cooldown Tech'. (gwaio_cooldown_bots.js:8)

Bot Engine Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card increases the movement speed of all mobile bots by 50%. Short title, noun phrase; 'Engine' is figurative (it is a speed upgrade). Must match the opening words of its description 'Bot Engine Tech increases speed of all bots by 50%'. (gwc_speed_bots.js:10)

Bot Engine Tech increases speed of all b.message: Bot Engine Tech increases speed of all bots by 50%
Bot Engine Tech increases speed of all b.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bot Engine Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies the movement, acceleration and turn rates of every mobile bot by 1.5. Keep 50% exactly; there is no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Engine Tech'. (gwc_speed_bots.js:8)

Bot Fabrication Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card cuts the metal build cost of every mobile bot by 25%. Short title, noun phrase; 'Fabrication' is the game's word for construction. Must match the opening words of its description 'Bot Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all bots by 25%'. (gwc_cost_bots.js:10)

Bot Fabrication Tech reduces metal build.message: Bot Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all bots by 25%
Bot Fabrication Tech reduces metal build.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bot Fabrication Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies build_metal_cost of every mobile bot by 0.75. 'Metal' is one of the game's two resources; use its standard translation. Keep 25% exactly; no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Fabrication Tech'. (gwc_cost_bots.js:8)

Bot Factory.description: Unit name from the tech-card "Which Units?" tooltip on the galaxy map (gw_play): the tooltip lists every unit a tech card affects, one name per line. This is a stock Planetary Annihilation unit; use the game's existing translation of that unit's display name so the tooltip matches the in-game build bar. Noun, singular, title case. The same English text is also registered as a race-specific unit name (race descriptor unitNames) for the Bugs/Exiles races, where the race's own unit has the same name; keep the two identical. (unit_names.js:36, exiles.js:454)

Bot Factory Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_botfactory, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Bot Factory"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Bot Factory Upgrade Tech enables the building of advanced units by basic bot manufacturing."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_botfactory.js)

Bot Factory Upgrade Tech enables the bui.message: Bot Factory Upgrade Tech enables the building of advanced units by basic bot manufacturing.
Bot Factory Upgrade Tech enables the bui.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Bot Factory Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. 'Basic bot manufacturing' means the basic Bot Factory building: after this card it can produce advanced (tier 2) bots. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bot Factory Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_botfactory.js:11)

Bounties.description: Game modifier name listed under "Game Modifiers" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), one per line, and in the win-conditions line of the in-game HUD (live_game), where modifiers are joined with " | ". "Bounties" = every kill earns an economy multiplier; in the HUD it may be followed by " x<value>". Noun, plural, no punctuation; must match "BOUNTIES" in the Game Modifiers tooltip and the "Bounties Chance" label. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:241, win_conditions_text.js:27)

Bounties Chance.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a percentage dropdown; tooltip: "Chance of a system awarding bounties for army kills." Title case (CSS up-cases it on screen), no trailing punctuation (the colon is outside the tag). Noun phrase; "Bounties" must match the modifier name. Sibling: "Bounty Value". (ai_settings.html:486)

Bounty Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card switches on the Bounties game modifier (kill an enemy commander, receive a resource bounty) in every battle of the war. Short title, noun phrase. 'Bounties' is a stock game mode name; use the game's existing translation. Must agree with the description 'Bounty tech enables the bounties game modifier in every system.' (gwaio_enable_bounties.js:9)

Bounty Value.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a dropdown of multipliers; tooltip: "Eco bonus per army kill." Title case (CSS up-cases it on screen), no trailing punctuation (the colon is outside the tag). Noun phrase, singular. (ai_settings.html:509)

Bounty tech enables the bounties game mo.message: Bounty tech enables the bounties game modifier in every system.
Bounty tech enables the bounties game mo.description: Body text of the tech card 'Bounty Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card turns on the stock 'Bounties' game modifier for every star system (battle) in the war. 'Bounties' should use the game's existing translation of that game mode. 'System' means a star system on the galaxy map. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bounty Tech' (English lower-cases 'tech' here; follow your locale's rule). (gwaio_enable_bounties.js:7)

Bronze.description:
Difficulty tier name for a Galactic War. Shown as the selected tier on the war setup screen (gw_start), in the "Difficulty:" row of the war-info panel on the galaxy map, in the co-op lobby title ("GWO Co-op - Difficulty: X"), and as the first part of the auto-generated war name (" - Players - - "). Noun, singular, title case, no punctuation. Must agree with the upper-cased tier name used in the difficulty tooltip ("BEGINNER: you completed the tutorial
CASUAL: ..."). The ten tiers are Beginner, Casual, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Uber, Custom. (difficulty_levels.js:89)

Buff Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started, as the locked-loadout tooltip while it is still locked, and afterwards as the first card in the Data Bank list on the galaxy map. This loadout gives all units 30% more health and damage but 25% less speed and 30% higher cost. Noun phrase, a title. 'Buff' is slang for strong/muscular (and a gaming term for a stat boost); render the sense of 'beefed-up', not a colour. Follow the pattern of the other '<X> Commander' loadout names. (tgw_start_tank.js:42)

Bugs.description: Name of the Bugs race (an alien unit set from the Bugs faction mod). Used as the heading of the neutral-system lore topic about the Bugs in the Planetary Intelligence panel, and as the race's name in race pickers, the AI modal table and the war-info panel. Proper noun, plural in English; keep the name the Bugs mod itself uses in the target locale (usually untranslated in Latin/Cyrillic/Chinese locales, transliterated in ja/ko). (lore.js:41, bugs.js:11)

Build faster.description: One of the AI buff names listed under "AI Tech" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), one per line. Means the enemy AI's units are built faster. Short verb phrase (comparative), no punctuation; keep parallel with the other buffs ("Costs decreased", "Damage increased", "Health increased", "Speed increased", "Commanders enhanced", "Combat units enhanced", "Factory cooldown decreased"). (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:181)

Bumblebee Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_bumblebee, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Bumblebee" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Bumblebee Upgrade Tech causes the carpet bomber to drop a mine instead of bombs."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_bumblebee.js)

Bumblebee Upgrade Tech causes the carpet.message: Bumblebee Upgrade Tech causes the carpet bomber to drop a mine instead of bombs.
Bumblebee Upgrade Tech causes the carpet.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Bumblebee Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. The Bumblebee is the game's basic carpet bomber; after the card its bomb deals no damage and instead leaves a land mine where it lands, and the player also gains the land mine unit. 'Mine' is an explosive land mine, not a resource mine. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Bumblebee Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_bumblebee.js:8)

Buried deep within the data banks of the.message: Buried deep within the data banks of the oldest commanders are references to the MLA. Some commanders believe that at one time all the factions fought as one against the Progenitors, while others dismiss this as heresy.
Buried deep within the data banks of the.description: Lore description for the neutral-system topic "The Machine Liberation Army" (the MLA, the base game's faction/unit set). Shown in the Planetary Intelligence panel for a neutral system when the "System Lore" game option is on. Full paragraph; "MLA" and "Progenitors" stay as the game's terms; keep the final full stop. (lore.js:23)

CASUAL: you have some hours in PA.message: CASUAL: you have some hours in PA
CASUAL: you have some hours in PA.description:
One line of the difficulty tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start): the "?" beside the Difficulty dropdown lists every difficulty level, one per line, as "LEVEL: who it suits". The upper-case word before the colon is the difficulty level's name as it appears in the dropdown; keep it as the game's own translation of that level renders it (uppercased) and keep the colon. The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) "PA" is the game's abbreviation, Planetary Annihilation; keep it.

CEO Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started, as the locked-loadout tooltip while it is still locked, and afterwards as the first card in the Data Bank list on the galaxy map. This loadout lets the player's commander build Colonel support commanders, armed with Uber Cannons, at half cost. Noun phrase, a title. 'CEO' is the corporate 'chief executive officer' joke (the commander delegates to subordinates); keep the acronym or use your locale's equivalent. Follow the pattern of the other '<X> Commander' loadout names. (gwaio_start_ceo.js:68)

CLUSTER: land. Uses Angels and Colonels.message: CLUSTER: land. Uses Angels and Colonels as Sub Commanders and cannot build them.
CLUSTER: land. Uses Angels and Colonels.description:
One line of the faction tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start), shown beside the Faction dropdown. Lines read "FACTION NAME: preferred unit class", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is one of the game's enemy factions (a proper noun; render it as the game's own translation does, uppercased) and the word after the colon is the unit class that faction favours (vehicles, air/navy, bots, orbital, land), using the game's stock wording for that class. Keep the colon; no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoFactionTooltip) This line is added only when TITANS is active. The Cluster is a TITANS-only faction; "land" means ground units. Angel and Colonel are unit names (proper nouns: keep untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales, transliterate in ja/ko as the game does); the Cluster fields them as Sub Commanders but cannot build more.

COMMANDER TRANSPORT:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before an on/off dropdown; tooltip: "Allow Commanders to travel by orbital transport and teleporter." Noun phrase, singular, upper-case; keep the trailing colon. (ai_settings.html:344)

CUSTOM: create your own challenge.description:
One line of the difficulty tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start): the "?" beside the Difficulty dropdown lists every difficulty level, one per line, as "LEVEL: who it suits". The upper-case word before the colon is the difficulty level's name as it appears in the dropdown; keep it as the game's own translation of that level renders it (uppercased) and keep the colon. The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) CUSTOM is the level that unlocks the AI Settings panel so the player sets each value.

Cancel.description: Button label on the post-battle "waiting for victory" overlay on the galaxy map (gw_play), shown to the co-op host while the game waits for all players to return; cancels the wait. Imperative verb, title case, no punctuation; use the game's standard "Cancel". (victory_wait.html:23)

Casual.description:
Difficulty tier name for a Galactic War. Shown as the selected tier on the war setup screen (gw_start), in the "Difficulty:" row of the war-info panel on the galaxy map, in the co-op lobby title ("GWO Co-op - Difficulty: X"), and as the first part of the auto-generated war name (" - Players - - "). Noun, singular, title case, no punctuation. Must agree with the upper-cased tier name used in the difficulty tooltip ("BEGINNER: you completed the tutorial
CASUAL: ..."). The ten tiers are Beginner, Casual, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Uber, Custom. (difficulty_levels.js:32)

Catalyst Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_catalyst, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Catalyst"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Catalyst Upgrade Tech doubles the health of the Catalyst and halves its cost."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_catalyst.js)

Catalyst Upgrade Tech doubles the health.message: Catalyst Upgrade Tech doubles the health of the Catalyst and halves its cost.
Catalyst Upgrade Tech doubles the health.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Catalyst Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. The card multiplies the Catalyst's max health by 2 and its metal build cost by 0.5. 'Catalyst' is a unit name; keep it as the game's unit tables have it. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Catalyst Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_catalyst.js:8)

Catapult Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_catapult, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Catapult" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Catapult Upgrade Tech adds flak from the Storm flak tank to the tactical missile launcher."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_catapult.js)

Catapult Upgrade Tech adds flak from the.message: Catapult Upgrade Tech adds flak from the Storm flak tank to the tactical missile launcher.
Catapult Upgrade Tech adds flak from the.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Catapult Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. The Catapult (tactical missile launcher structure) gains the flak anti-air weapon of the Storm (a mobile flak vehicle) and counts as air defence. 'Storm' and 'Catapult' are unit names; keep them as the game's unit tables have them. 'Flak' is anti-aircraft fire. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Catapult Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_catapult.js:8)

Cautious.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel of the galaxy map (gw_play) and in the war-info panel. Adjective or noun used as a label, singular, no punctuation. A penchant word (Artillery, Fortress, Assault...) may be appended after it with a space, so keep it short. The same trait key is shared by all four stock factions and the Cluster faction; translate it once. (gw_faction_0.js:72 and the other faction files, cluster_faction.js:36)

Chance of a system allowing you to land.message: Chance of a system allowing you to land outside spawn zones.
Chance of a system allowing you to land.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "LAND ANYWHERE CHANCE:" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Land" = choose a starting position at the beginning of a battle; "spawn zones" = the normal fixed landing areas. Full sentence; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:443)

Chance of a system awarding bounties for.message: Chance of a system awarding bounties for army kills.
Chance of a system awarding bounties for.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "Bounties Chance" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Army kills" = killing enemy armies' units. Full sentence; keep the full stop; "bounties" must match the modifier name. (ai_settings.html:489)

Chance of an allied Commander being pres.message: Chance of an allied Commander being present in a system.
Chance of an allied Commander being pres.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "ALLY CHANCE:" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Full sentence; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:420)

Chance of eradication mode being enabled.message: Chance of eradication mode being enabled.
Chance of eradication mode being enabled.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "ERADICATION CHANCE:" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Eradication mode" is the game modifier shown as "Eradicate" on the galaxy map (all units of chosen types must be destroyed to win). Full sentence; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:531)

Chance of more than one faction being pr.message: Chance of more than one faction being present in a system.
Chance of more than one faction being pr.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "FFA Chance" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. FFA = free-for-all, i.e. several enemy factions fighting each other in one system. Full sentence; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:397)

Chance per system of a Commander death i.message: Chance per system of a Commander death in a battle defeating all Commanders of that faction in the system.
Chance per system of a Commander death i.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "SUDDEN DEATH CHANCE:" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Describes the Sudden Death modifier. Full sentence; keep the full stop; "Commander" is the player/AI's hero unit. (ai_settings.html:466)

Chrono Cam.description: In-game pause menu (live_game) button label; opens the Chrono Cam replay/time-rewind view. Uses the base game's existing "Chrono Cam" entry, so match that translation. Proper noun, no punctuation. (menu.js:59)

Co-Op Settings.description: Sub-heading in the war-info panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), visible only in a co-op war, over the table of co-op rows (Scaling For:, Armies:, Tech:, Player Slots:). Noun phrase, plural, title case, no punctuation. (gwo_panel.html:70)

Co-op host setup.description: Prefix for a launch-progress stage message shown to the co-op host while a battle is being prepared: assembled as "<this string>: <stage text>" for the second (host-only) setup pass. Noun phrase used as a heading; no punctuation of its own (the code adds the colon and a space after it, so word order is fixed). Sibling: "Co-op shared setup" for the first pass. (referee.js:62)

Co-op shared setup.description: Prefix for a launch-progress stage message shown to the co-op host while a battle is being prepared: assembled as "<this string>: <stage text>" for the first setup pass, which is shared with all players. Noun phrase used as a heading; no punctuation of its own (the code appends a colon and a space). Sibling: "Co-op host setup". (referee.js:61)

Colonel.description: Unit name used as an eradication target: listed after "Eradicate:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map and in the in-game HUD win-conditions line ("Eradicate: Commander, Colonel, Factory, Fabber"), meaning the enemy's Sub Commander units must all be destroyed. "Colonel" is the stock name of the Sub Commander unit; use the game's translation of that unit. Noun, singular, no punctuation. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:140, win_conditions_text.js:16)

Colonel Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_colonel, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Colonel" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Colonel Upgrade Tech causes support commanders to explode on death."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_colonel.js)

Colonel Upgrade Tech causes support comm.message: Colonel Upgrade Tech causes support commanders to explode on death.
Colonel Upgrade Tech causes support comm.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Colonel Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. 'Support commanders' is the class name of the Colonel unit: the card gives it the commander's death explosion (ground and air variants). The opening words must match the translated card name 'Colonel Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_colonel.js:8)

Combat units enhanced.description: One of the AI buff names listed under "AI Tech" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play). Means the enemy AI's combat units have improved stats. Short phrase, no punctuation; keep parallel with "Commanders enhanced" and the other buff names. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:187)

Commander.description: Standalone noun, singular: the player's Commander unit. It is reused in six places, so keep it a plain noun without an article. (1) It is joined with the separate string 'Naval' as 'Naval' + ' ' + 'Commander' to form the name of the Naval Commander loadout card on the loadout picker and in the Data Bank list, so it must be the word that can follow 'Naval' in your language. (2) It is the unit name in the mod's own unit-name table. (3) It is the label of the button that opens the commander-model picker on the Galactic War start screen and the title of that picker dialog. (4) It is the first item in the 'Eradicate: Commander, Colonel, Factory, Fabber' target list shown on the galaxy map and in the in-battle win-conditions text. Use the game's own stock translation of 'Commander'. (gwaio_start_naval.js:18; section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:137; unit_names.js:22; commander_button.html:6; commander_modal.html:14; win_conditions_text.js:14)

Commander Ammunition Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card raises the damage of every commander weapon (including Sub Commanders) by 25%. Short title, noun phrase; 'Ammunition' is figurative for a damage upgrade. Must match the opening words of its description 'Commander Ammunition Tech increases damage of your commanders by 25%'. (gwc_damage_commander.js:10)

Commander Ammunition Tech increases dama.message: Commander Ammunition Tech increases damage of your commanders by 25%
Commander Ammunition Tech increases dama.description: Body text of the tech card 'Commander Ammunition Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies the damage and splash damage of all commander ammunition by 1.25. 'Commanders' is plural because Sub Commanders benefit too. Keep 25% exactly; no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Commander Ammunition Tech'. (gwc_damage_commander.js:8)

Commander Armor Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card doubles the player's commander's max health. Short title, noun phrase. Must match the opening words of its description 'Commander Armor Tech increases the health of your commanders by 100%.' (gwc_health_commander.js:10)

Commander Armor Tech increases the healt.message: Commander Armor Tech increases the health of your commanders by 100%.
Commander Armor Tech increases the healt.description: Body text of the tech card 'Commander Armor Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies the commander's max_health by 2. Keep 100% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Commander Armor Tech'. (gwc_health_commander.js:8)

Commander Combat Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card triples commander speed, doubles commander health and raises commander weapon damage by 25%. Short title, noun phrase. Must match the opening words of its description 'Commander Combat Tech increases the speed of your commanders by 200%...'. (gwc_combat_commander.js:11)

Commander Combat Tech increases the spee.message: Commander Combat Tech increases the speed of your commanders by 200%, doubles commander health, and increases damage by 25%.
Commander Combat Tech increases the spee.description: Body text of the tech card 'Commander Combat Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies the commander's movement rates by 3 (i.e. +200%), its max health by 2 and the damage of all commander ammunition by 1.25. Keep 200% and 25% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Commander Combat Tech'. (gwc_combat_commander.js:9)

Commander Engine Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card doubles the commander's movement speed. Short title, noun phrase; 'Engine' is figurative (it is a speed upgrade). Must match the opening words of its description 'Commander Engine Tech increases the speed of your commanders by 100%.' (gwc_speed_commander.js:10)

Commander Engine Tech increases the spee.message: Commander Engine Tech increases the speed of your commanders by 100%.
Commander Engine Tech increases the spee.description: Body text of the tech card 'Commander Engine Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies the commander's movement, acceleration and turn rates by 2. Keep 100% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Commander Engine Tech'. (gwc_speed_commander.js:8)

Commander Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_ubercannon_structure, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Commander"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Commander Upgrade Tech increases Uber Cannon damage by 300% and allows you to reclaim friendly Commanders for metal."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_ubercannon_structure.js)

Commander Upgrade Tech increases Uber Ca.message: Commander Upgrade Tech increases Uber Cannon damage by 300% and allows you to reclaim friendly Commanders for metal.
Commander Upgrade Tech increases Uber Ca.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Commander Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. The card multiplies the damage, splash and burn damage of the commander's secondary weapon (the Uber Cannon) by 4 (i.e. +300%) and adds friendly commanders to what every fabricator build arm may reclaim. 'Uber Cannon' is the stock name of the commander's big secondary weapon; use the game's existing translation. 'Reclaim' is the game's term for recycling a unit back into metal. Keep 300% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Commander Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_ubercannon_structure.js:9)

Commanders.description: Section header on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Heads the block with "Boss Commanders" and "ARMIES/COMMANDERS:". Noun, plural, title case, no punctuation; a Commander is the player's/AI's hero unit. (ai_settings.html:58)

Commanders enhanced.description: One of the AI buff names listed under "AI Tech" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play). Means the enemy AI's Commander units have improved stats. Short phrase, no punctuation; keep parallel with "Combat units enhanced" and the other buff names. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:184)

Commanders on the fringes of the galaxy.message: Commanders on the fringes of the galaxy speak of a new force not of the four factions with units of many origins. It is rumoured that their forces include organics.
Commanders on the fringes of the galaxy.description: Lore description for the neutral-system topic "The Union" (the Exiles race, a unit set mixing many origins). Shown in the Planetary Intelligence panel for a neutral system when the "System Lore" option is on. Full paragraph; "organics" = living creatures as opposed to machines; keep the final full stop. (lore.js:33)

Complete Air Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card unlocks every air unit and both air factories at once, plus the advanced starter structures. Short title, noun phrase; 'Complete' is an adjective meaning 'the whole air tech tree', not a verb. Keep it parallel with the sibling names 'Complete Bot Tech', 'Complete Naval Tech', 'Complete Orbital Tech', 'Complete Vehicle Tech', 'Complete Energy Tech'. Must match the opening words of its description 'Complete air tech enables building of all mobile air units and factories...'. (gwc_enable_air_all.js:11)

Complete Basic Factory Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card unlocks all three basic land factories (air, bot, vehicle) together with their basic units. Short title, noun phrase; 'Complete' is an adjective (the whole basic tier), 'Basic' is the game's word for tier 1. Note its description begins 'Complete Basic Tech' (without 'Factory'); keep the two recognisably the same card. (gwaio_enable_factories_t1_all.js:11)

Complete Basic Tech enables building of.message: Complete Basic Tech enables building of basic air, bot, and vehicle units and factories. Basic factories are built via your commander or any basic fabricator.
Complete Basic Tech enables building of.description: Body text of the tech card 'Complete Basic Factory Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card adds every basic (tier 1) air, bot and vehicle unit and factory to the player's tech. The second sentence tells the player who can build those factories: the commander or any basic fabricator. 'Basic' is the game's word for tier 1 and 'fabricator' for a construction unit; use the game's own terms. The opening words should echo the translated card name 'Complete Basic Factory Tech'. (gwaio_enable_factories_t1_all.js:9)

Complete Bot Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card unlocks every bot and both bot factories at once, plus the advanced starter structures. Short title, noun phrase; 'Complete' is an adjective meaning the whole bot tech tree. Keep it parallel with the other 'Complete <X> Tech' names. Must match the opening words of its description 'Complete Bot tech enables building of all Bots and all Bot Factories...'. (gwc_enable_bots_all.js:11)

Complete Bot tech enables building of al.message: Complete Bot tech enables building of all Bots and all Bot Factories. Basic Bot factories are built via your commander or any basic fabricator. Advanced Bot factories are built via basic or advanced bot fabricators.
Complete Bot tech enables building of al.description: Body text of the tech card 'Complete Bot Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card adds every bot unit and both bot factories (basic and advanced) to the player's tech. Sentences two and three tell the player which builders can place each factory tier. 'Basic' and 'Advanced' are the game's words for tier 1 and tier 2, 'fabricator' for a construction unit; use the game's own terms. The English capitalisation of 'Bots' and 'Bot Factories' is inconsistent and need not be copied. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Complete Bot Tech'. (gwc_enable_bots_all.js:9)

Complete Energy Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card cuts the energy drain of radar/intel structures, energy weapons and teleporters by 75% each. Short title, noun phrase; 'Complete' is an adjective (all three energy-saving techs in one). Keep it parallel with the other 'Complete <X> Tech' names. Must match the opening words of its description. (gwc_energy_efficiency_all.js:11)

Complete Energy Tech reduces energy cost.message: Complete Energy Tech reduces energy costs for intelligence structures by 75%, weapon energy costs by 75%, and teleport energy costs by 75%.
Complete Energy Tech reduces energy cost.description: Body text of the tech card 'Complete Energy Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies energy consumption of intelligence structures (radar, jammers and similar), the energy demand of energy-based weapons, and teleporter energy demand each by 0.25. Keep the three 75% figures exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Complete Energy Tech'. (gwc_energy_efficiency_all.js:9)

Complete Naval Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card unlocks every naval unit and both naval factories at once, plus the advanced starter structures. Short title, noun phrase; 'Complete' is an adjective meaning the whole naval tech tree. Keep it parallel with the other 'Complete <X> Tech' names. Must match the opening words of its description. (gwc_enable_sea_all.js:11)

Complete Naval Tech enables building of.message: Complete Naval Tech enables building of all naval units and all naval factories. Basic naval factories are built via your commander or any basic fabricator. Advanced naval factories are built via basic or advanced naval fabricators.
Complete Naval Tech enables building of.description: Body text of the tech card 'Complete Naval Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card adds every naval unit and both naval factories (basic and advanced) to the player's tech. Sentences two and three tell the player which builders can place each factory tier. 'Basic' and 'Advanced' are the game's words for tier 1 and tier 2, 'fabricator' for a construction unit; use the game's own terms. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Complete Naval Tech'. (gwc_enable_sea_all.js:9)

Complete Orbital Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card unlocks every orbital unit plus the Orbital Launcher and Orbital Factory. Short title, noun phrase; 'Complete' is an adjective meaning the whole orbital tech tree. Keep it parallel with the other 'Complete <X> Tech' names. Must match the opening words of its description. (gwc_enable_orbital_all.js:11)

Complete Orbital Tech enables building o.message: Complete Orbital Tech enables building of all orbital units and all orbital Factories. Orbital launchers are built by any basic fabricator. Orbital factories are built via an orbital fabricator.
Complete Orbital Tech enables building o.description: Body text of the tech card 'Complete Orbital Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card adds every orbital unit and both orbital production buildings to the player's tech. Sentences two and three tell the player who builds them: 'Orbital Launcher' and 'Orbital Factory' are stock building names; use the game's existing translations. The English capital in 'orbital Factories' is a typo and need not be copied. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Complete Orbital Tech'. (gwc_enable_orbital_all.js:9)

Complete Vehicle Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card unlocks every vehicle and both vehicle factories at once, plus the advanced starter structures. Short title, noun phrase; 'Complete' is an adjective meaning the whole vehicle tech tree. 'Vehicle' is the game's name for the tank/wheeled land unit class. Keep it parallel with the other 'Complete <X> Tech' names. Must match the opening words of its description. (gwc_enable_vehicles_all.js:11)

Complete Vehicle tech enables building o.message: Complete Vehicle tech enables building of all Vehicle and all Vehicle Factories. Basic Vehicle factories are built via your commander or any basic fabricator. Advanced Vehicle factories are built via basic or advanced vehicle fabricators.
Complete Vehicle tech enables building o.description: Body text of the tech card 'Complete Vehicle Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card adds every vehicle unit and both vehicle factories (basic and advanced) to the player's tech. Sentences two and three tell the player which builders can place each factory tier. 'All Vehicle' in English is a typo for 'all Vehicles'; translate it as plural. 'Basic' and 'Advanced' are the game's words for tier 1 and tier 2, 'fabricator' for a construction unit. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Complete Vehicle Tech'. (gwc_enable_vehicles_all.js:9)

Complete air tech enables building of al.message: Complete air tech enables building of all mobile air units and factories. Basic air factories are built via your commander or any basic fabricator. Advanced factories are built via a basic or advanced air fabricator.
Complete air tech enables building of al.description: Body text of the tech card 'Complete Air Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card adds every aircraft and both air factories (basic and advanced) to the player's tech. Sentences two and three tell the player which builders can place each factory tier. 'Basic' and 'Advanced' are the game's words for tier 1 and tier 2, 'fabricator' for a construction unit; use the game's own terms. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Complete Air Tech' (English lower-cases 'air tech' here; follow your locale's rule). (gwc_enable_air_all.js:9)

Configure campaign options..description: Intro sentence under the title of the Game Options modal on the war setup screen (gw_start), above the switches (Hardcore, Faction Scaling, Easy Systems...). Imperative sentence; keep the full stop. (difficulty_options.html:27)

Contains 16 data banks. Alas, travelling.message: Contains 16 data banks. Alas, travelling light means you start with only the most basic of bots.
Contains 16 data banks. Alas, travelling.description: Body text of the starting loadout card 'Backpacker Commander', shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started and in the Data Bank card list afterwards. 'Data banks' are GWO's name for tech card slots: this loadout gives 16 slots (12 more than usual) but only the basic bot factory, basic bot fabricator and the Dox bot. Keep the number 16. 'Alas' and 'travelling light' set a wry tone (a backpacker carries little); keep it light. Use the same translation of 'Data Bank' as the rest of the mod. (gwaio_start_backpacker.js:24)

Contains every factory on every tier of.message: Contains every factory on every tier of the tech tree.
Contains every factory on every tier of.description: Body text of the starting loadout card 'Hoarder Commander', shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started and in the Data Bank card list afterwards. The loadout adds every air, bot, naval, orbital and vehicle unit, so all basic and advanced factories are available from the first battle. 'Tier' refers to basic (tier 1) and advanced (tier 2). Plain statement, no unit names. (gwaio_start_hoarder.js:31)

Contains no basic land or air factories,.message: Contains no basic land or air factories, just Lobs and Unit Cannons built by the commander. Halves the cost of both. All land units can be built from the Unit Cannon as they are unlocked.
Contains no basic land or air factories,.description: Body text of the starting loadout card 'Paratrooper Commander', shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started and in the Data Bank card list afterwards. The loadout removes the normal basic factories; the commander instead builds the Lob (a small unit-launching artillery) and the Unit Cannon (the large unit-launching structure), both at half metal cost, and every land unit the player later unlocks becomes launchable from the Unit Cannon. 'Lob' and 'Unit Cannon' are unit names: leave them untranslated in Latin/Cyrillic/Chinese locales and transliterate in ja/ko as the game's own unit tables do. 'Lobs' is the plural of the unit name. (gwaio_start_paratrooper.js:93)

Continue Tutorial.description: In-game pause menu (live_game) button label shown instead of "Continue War" when the battle is the Galactic War tutorial: returns to the galaxy map after the battle ends. Uses the base game's existing entry; imperative verb phrase, title case, no punctuation. (menu.js:27)

Continue War.description: In-game pause menu (live_game) button label shown once the battle is over: returns to the galaxy map to continue the Galactic War. Uses the base game's existing entry; imperative verb phrase, title case, no punctuation. (menu.js:28)

Costs decreased.description: One of the AI buff names listed under "AI Tech" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play). Means the enemy AI's units cost less. Short phrase (noun + past participle), no punctuation; keep parallel with "Damage increased", "Health increased", "Speed increased", "Factory cooldown decreased". (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:169)

Custom.description:
Difficulty tier name for a Galactic War. Shown as the selected tier on the war setup screen (gw_start), in the "Difficulty:" row of the war-info panel on the galaxy map, in the co-op lobby title ("GWO Co-op - Difficulty: X"), and as the first part of the auto-generated war name (" - Players - - "). Noun, singular, title case, no punctuation. Must agree with the upper-cased tier name used in the difficulty tooltip ("BEGINNER: you completed the tutorial
CASUAL: ..."). The ten tiers are Beginner, Casual, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Uber, Custom. "Custom" is the tier where the player sets every AI Settings value by hand; adjective used as a name. (difficulty_levels.js:263)

DIAMOND: your loadouts are OP.description:
One line of the difficulty tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start): the "?" beside the Difficulty dropdown lists every difficulty level, one per line, as "LEVEL: who it suits". The upper-case word before the colon is the difficulty level's name as it appears in the dropdown; keep it as the game's own translation of that level renders it (uppercased) and keep the colon. The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) "OP" is gaming slang for overpowered; a loadout is the player's starting Commander kit (use the stock translation of Loadout).

Damage increased.description: One of the AI buff names listed under "AI Tech" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play). Means the enemy AI's units deal more damage. Short phrase, no punctuation; parallel with "Health increased", "Speed increased", "Costs decreased". (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:172)

Data Bank holds one Tech. Explore system.message: Data Bank holds one Tech. Explore systems to find new Tech.
Data Bank holds one Tech. Explore system.description: Description text of an empty Data Bank slot in the tech-card inventory on the galaxy map (gw_play), shown when the slot holds no card; its title is "Empty Data Bank". "Data Bank" is the game's name for an inventory slot and "Tech" for a tech card; use the base game's translations of both. Two sentences; keep the full stops. (cards.js:224)

Deck:.description: Row label in the war-info panel on the galaxy map (gw_play); the value beside it is the name of the tech-card deck in use ("Basic", "Galactic War Overhaul" or a mod deck). "Deck" as in a deck of cards; noun, singular; keep the trailing colon. (gwo_panel.html:45)

Default Commander.description: Name of the base starting card that every Galactic War loadout is built on, shown as the first card in the Data Bank card list on the galaxy map when no special loadout was chosen. It supplies the commander plus the basic economy, defence, intel, naval and orbital structures and the teleporter. Noun phrase, a title: 'Default' means the standard, unmodified loadout. Follow the pattern of the other '<X> Commander' loadout names. (gwc_start.js:10)

Defender.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel of the galaxy map (gw_play) and in the war-info panel. Adjective or noun used as a label, singular, no punctuation. A penchant word (Artillery, Fortress, Assault...) may be appended after it with a space, so keep it short. The same trait key is shared by all four stock factions and the Cluster faction; translate it once. "Defender" = builds defences and holds ground; noun. (gw_faction_0.js:53 and the other faction files, cluster_faction.js:33)

Defense Ammunition Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card raises the damage of every defensive structure's weapon by 25%. Short title, noun phrase; 'Ammunition' is figurative for a damage upgrade. US spelling 'Defense'. Must match the opening words of its description 'Defense Ammunition Tech increases damage of all defensive structures by 25%'. (gwc_damage_defenses.js:11)

Defense Ammunition Tech increases damage.message: Defense Ammunition Tech increases damage of all defensive structures by 25%
Defense Ammunition Tech increases damage.description: Body text of the tech card 'Defense Ammunition Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies the damage and splash damage of every defence structure's ammunition by 1.25. 'Defensive structures' means turrets, anti-air, artillery and similar static defences. Keep 25% exactly; no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Defense Ammunition Tech'. (gwc_damage_defenses.js:9)

Defense Fabrication Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card halves the metal cost of every defensive structure. Short title, noun phrase; 'Fabrication' is the game's word for construction. US spelling 'Defense'. Must match the opening words of its description 'Defense Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all defensive structures by 50%'. (gwc_cost_defenses.js:11)

Defense Fabrication Tech reduces metal b.message: Defense Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all defensive structures by 50%
Defense Fabrication Tech reduces metal b.description: Body text of the tech card 'Defense Fabrication Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies build_metal_cost of every defence structure by 0.5. 'Metal' is one of the game's two resources; use its standard translation. Keep 50% exactly; no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Defense Fabrication Tech'. (gwc_cost_defenses.js:9)

Defense Tech Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout card, shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started, as the locked-loadout tooltip while it is still locked, and afterwards as the first card in the Data Bank list on the galaxy map. This loadout makes defensive structures cheaper, faster-firing, longer-ranged and quicker-turning, and lets the commander and basic fabricators build all of them. Noun phrase, a title: a commander specialised in defence tech. US spelling 'Defense'. Follow the pattern of the other '<X> Commander' loadout names. (nem_start_tower_rush.js:89)

Defenses are 50% cheaper, fire 25% faste.message: Defenses are 50% cheaper, fire 25% faster, have 50% more range, and turn 300% quicker. Barriers are 90% cheaper and have their health doubled. All defenses can be built by both the commander and basic fabricators.
Defenses are 50% cheaper, fire 25% faste.description: Body text of the starting loadout card 'Defense Tech Commander', shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started and in the Data Bank card list afterwards. The loadout multiplies defence structure cost by 0.5, their weapons' rate of fire by 1.25, range by 1.5 and turret turn rate by 4 (i.e. +300%); walls cost 0.1 of normal with 2x health; and every defence structure, including advanced ones, becomes buildable by the commander and basic fabricators. 'Barriers' means the Wall structure. Keep 50%, 25%, 50%, 300% and 90% exactly. US spelling 'Defenses'. (nem_start_tower_rush.js:94)

Delay before AI realises it cannot expan.message: Delay before AI realises it cannot expand.
Delay before AI realises it cannot expan.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "Unable To Expand Delay" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Expand" = build new bases on more territory. Full sentence; keep the full stop; British spelling "realises" may be normalised. (ai_settings.html:256)

Delay in creating new bases..description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "NEW BASE DELAY:" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sentence fragment; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:238)

Delete Tech.description: Button label under a card in the tech-card inventory on the galaxy map (gw_play): discards the selected Tech card from the Data Bank. Imperative verb + noun; "Tech" = tech card, use the base game's word. Title case, no punctuation. (cards_inventory.html:22)

Deployed by covert Hegemony forces for t.message: Deployed by covert Hegemony forces for the duration of the Century War, their current level of proliferation indicates that they developed the ability to seed planets on their own after the war ended, or as a desperate attempt by the Xziphid to stave off defeat.
Deployed by covert Hegemony forces for t.description: Lore description for the neutral-system topic "Bugs" (the Bugs alien race). Shown in the Planetary Intelligence panel for a neutral system when the "System Lore" option is on. Full paragraph; Hegemony, Century War and Xziphid are proper nouns from the Bugs mod's fiction, keep them; keep the final full stop. (lore.js:43)

Diamond.description:
Difficulty tier name for a Galactic War. Shown as the selected tier on the war setup screen (gw_start), in the "Difficulty:" row of the war-info panel on the galaxy map, in the co-op lobby title ("GWO Co-op - Difficulty: X"), and as the first part of the auto-generated war name (" - Players - - "). Noun, singular, title case, no punctuation. Must agree with the upper-cased tier name used in the difficulty tooltip ("BEGINNER: you completed the tutorial
CASUAL: ..."). The ten tiers are Beginner, Casual, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Uber, Custom. (difficulty_levels.js:205)

Difficulty:.description: Row label in the war-info panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), followed by the difficulty tier name (Beginner, Casual, Iron...). Also used to build the co-op lobby title "GWO Co-op - Difficulty: <tier>", where the tier name follows after a space, so the colon must stay at the end and the label must read naturally before the value. Noun, singular; keep the trailing colon. (gwo_panel.html:26, gwo_panel.js:34)

Display the original pre-release Galacti.message: Display the original pre-release Galactic War lore in the Planetary Intelligence panel.
Display the original pre-release Galacti.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "System Lore" switch in the Game Options modal on the war setup screen (gw_start). "Planetary Intelligence" is the name of the system-info panel on the galaxy map; match its heading. Full sentence; keep the full stop. (difficulty_options.html:159)

Distance examined when choosing spawn..description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "Landing Evaluation" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Spawn" = the AI's starting position on the planet. Sentence fragment; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:326)

Dox Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_dox, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Dox" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Dox Upgrade Tech replaces the basic infantry's bullet weapons with flamethrowers."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_dox.js)

Dox Upgrade Tech replaces the basic infa.message: Dox Upgrade Tech replaces the basic infantry's bullet weapons with flamethrowers.
Dox Upgrade Tech replaces the basic infa.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Dox Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. 'The basic infantry' is the Dox bot. The card changes its ammo to a beam with 10x damage, cuts its range to 27% and adds flame muzzle effects, so it fights like a flamethrower. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Dox Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_dox.js:8)

Dragoon.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel of the galaxy map (gw_play) and in the war-info panel.
