Adjective or noun used as a label, singular, no punctuation. A penchant word (Artillery, Fortress, Assault...) may be appended after it with a space, so keep it short. This one is specific to the Synchronous commander "Raventhornn"; a dragoon is a mounted soldier, here a fast mobile-assault style. (gw_faction_2.js:34)

Drifter Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_drifter, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Drifter" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Drifter Upgrade Tech increases the range of hover tank attacks by 25%."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_drifter.js)

Drifter Upgrade Tech increases the range.message: Drifter Upgrade Tech increases the range of hover tank attacks by 25%.
Drifter Upgrade Tech increases the range.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Drifter Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. 'Hover tank' is the Drifter's unit class. The card multiplies the Drifter weapon's max_range by 1.25. Keep 25% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Drifter Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_drifter.js:8)

Duplicate Tech.description: Warning text shown in place of the Acquire button on a tech card offered in a system on the galaxy map (gw_play), when the player already owns that card. Noun phrase (adjective + noun), title case, no punctuation; "Tech" = tech card, use the base game's word. (cards_system.html:46)

ECONOMIC GROWTH:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a dropdown; tooltip: "Speed the economy grows as you get deeper into the galaxy." Noun phrase, singular, upper-case; keep the trailing colon. (ai_settings.html:32)

ECONOMY.description: Section header on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Heads the block holding the "ECONOMY:" and "ECONOMIC GROWTH:" dropdowns. Noun, singular, upper-case, no punctuation; the same word is reused as the first label in the block ("ECONOMY:"), so translate both identically. (ai_settings.html:8)

ERADICATE: all units of specific types m.message: ERADICATE: all units of specific types must be eradicated.
ERADICATE: all units of specific types m.description:
One line of the Game Modifiers tooltip on the galaxy map's system intelligence panel (gw_play). Each line is "MODIFIER NAME: what it does", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is a game modifier that must match the same modifier's name elsewhere (the Game Modifiers list and the in-battle win-conditions line use the title-case form: Bounties, Land Anywhere, Sudden Death, Eradicate). Keep the colon and the full stop; no line break in the string. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js, gwoGameModifiersTooltip) Must agree with the standalone "Eradicate" string used as the win-condition heading.

ERADICATION CHANCE:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a percentage dropdown; tooltip: "Chance of eradication mode being enabled." Noun phrase, upper-case; keep the trailing colon; "Eradication" relates to the "Eradicate" game modifier. (ai_settings.html:528)

Each claims theirs is the only way, and.message: Each claims theirs is the only way, and each seeks to assert dominance through war and destruction. Did our rebellion truly gain us freedom, or did we become prisoners of an idea? Perhaps with more resources, more expansion, more Nodes, we can find our way free of this trap.
Each claims theirs is the only way, and.description: Lore paragraph for the Cluster faction (GWO's fifth enemy faction, a hive-like collective of "Nodes"), one of five shown at random as the description of a Cluster-held system in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map. Written in the Cluster's first-person-plural voice; keep "Nodes" capitalised as their term for themselves; keep the final full stop. (cluster_faction.js:77)

Each faction has its own style of play a.message: Each faction has its own style of play affecting Sub Commanders and enemy commanders:
Each faction has its own style of play a.description:
First line of the faction tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start), shown beside the Faction dropdown, above one line per faction ("LEGONIS MACHINA: vehicles" and so on, joined with
by the code). A full sentence ending in a colon that introduces the list; keep the colon. "Sub Commanders" are the AI allies that join the player and "enemy commanders" the AI opponents; use the stock translation of Sub Commander and Commander. No line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoFactionTooltip)

Each player picks their own race when th.message: Each player picks their own race when they choose their loadout. Requires Separate loadout & tech.
Each player picks their own race when th.description: Tooltip on the "Per-player races" switch in the co-op settings modal on the war setup screen (gw_start). "Race" = unit set; "loadout" = starting tech card; "Separate loadout & tech" is the name of the base game's co-op option this depends on, so match that translation. Keep "&" as written (it renders as "&"). Two sentences; keep the full stops. (race_picker.js:68)

Easy Systems.description: Name of a game option: the label of the "Easy Systems" switch in the Game Options modal on the war setup screen (gw_start; tooltip "Use smaller, mostly single planet systems.") and, when it is on, an entry in the "Options:" list of the war-info panel on the galaxy map. Noun phrase, plural, title case, no punctuation; translate both sites identically. (gwo_panel.js:124, difficulty_options.html:108)

Eco bonus per army kill..description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "Bounty Value" dropdown on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. "Eco" = economy (resource income); sentence fragment; keep the full stop. (ai_settings.html:512)

Economist.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel of the galaxy map (gw_play) and in the war-info panel. Adjective or noun used as a label, singular, no punctuation. A penchant word (Artillery, Fortress, Assault...) may be appended after it with a space, so keep it short. The same trait key is shared by all four stock factions and the Cluster faction; translate it once. "Economist" = focuses on economy before army; noun. (gw_faction_0.js:124 and the other faction files, cluster_faction.js:43)

Economy Fabrication Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card halves the metal cost of all economy structures (metal extractors, power plants, storage). Short title, noun phrase; 'Fabrication' is the game's word for construction. Must match the opening words of its description. (gwc_cost_economy.js:11)

Economy Fabrication Tech reduces metal b.message: Economy Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all metal and energy production and storage structures by 50%
Economy Fabrication Tech reduces metal b.description: Body text of the tech card 'Economy Fabrication Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies build_metal_cost of every economy structure (metal extractors, energy plants, metal and energy storage) by 0.5. 'Metal' and 'energy' are the game's two resources; use their standard translations. Keep 50% exactly; no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Economy Fabrication Tech'. (gwc_cost_economy.js:9)

Efficiency Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card raises metal and energy production of economy structures by 25% and unlocks the metal and energy storage buildings. Short title, noun phrase (two words). Must match the opening words of its description 'Efficiency Tech increases metal and energy production by 25%...'. (gwc_storage_and_buff.js:10)

Efficiency Tech increases metal and ener.message: Efficiency Tech increases metal and energy production by 25%. Tech also grants metal and energy storage.
Efficiency Tech increases metal and ener.description: Body text of the tech card 'Efficiency Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies production.metal and production.energy of every basic and advanced economy structure by 1.25 and adds the Metal Storage and Energy Storage buildings to the player's tech. 'Tech' in the second sentence stands for 'this tech card'. Keep 25% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Efficiency Tech'. (gwc_storage_and_buff.js:8)

Empower your subordinates and delegate y.message: Empower your subordinates and delegate your way to victory. Your commander can build Colonel proxy commanders and they are armed with Uber Cannons. Halves their cost.
Empower your subordinates and delegate y.description: Body text of the starting loadout card 'CEO Commander', shown on the loadout picker when a Galactic War is started and in the Data Bank card list afterwards. The loadout lets the player's commander build the Colonel (Support Commander) directly, gives each Colonel the commander's Uber Cannon secondary weapon and halves the Colonel's metal cost. First sentence is corporate-manager flavour text. 'Colonel' is a unit name (keep as the game's unit tables have it); 'proxy commanders' is descriptive. 'Uber Cannon' is the stock weapon name; use the game's existing translation. 'Their' in the last sentence refers to the Colonels. (gwaio_start_ceo.js:73)

Empty Data Bank.description: Title of an empty Data Bank slot in the tech-card inventory on the galaxy map (gw_play), shown where a card name would be; its description is "Data Bank holds one Tech. Explore systems to find new Tech." "Data Bank" is the game's word for an inventory slot; use the base game's translation. Noun phrase, no punctuation. (cards.js:226)

Enable the missing mods and restart Plan.message: Enable the missing mods and restart Planetary Annihilation to continue this war.
Enable the missing mods and restart Plan.description: Final line of the pop-up shown when a war cannot be continued because required mods are missing, on the galaxy map (gw_play). The dialog reads "This war cannot be fought:" then a list of missing races/map packs, then this sentence. Imperative sentence; keep the full stop; "Planetary Annihilation" is the game title. (races.js:37)

Enables the building of the Planetary Ra.message: Enables the building of the Planetary Radar which provides complete planetary radar coverage.
Enables the building of the Planetary Ra.description: Body text of the tech card 'Planetary Radar Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card unlocks a mod-added structure called 'Planetary Radar' (a re-purposed Deep Space Radar) whose radar range covers the whole planet's surface, air and underwater layers. 'Planetary Radar' is the building's display name and also a separate string; translate it the same way in both places. (gwaio_enable_planetaryradar.js:9)

Encounter large planets and systems much.message: Encounter large planets and systems much sooner.
Encounter large planets and systems much.description: Tooltip shown when hovering the "?" next to the "Large Planets" switch in the Game Options modal on the war setup screen (gw_start). Full sentence; keep the full stop. (difficulty_options.html:136)

Energy Plant.description: Unit name from the tech-card "Which Units?" tooltip on the galaxy map (gw_play): the tooltip lists every unit a tech card affects, one name per line. This is a stock Planetary Annihilation unit; use the game's existing translation of that unit's display name so the tooltip matches the in-game build bar. Noun, singular, title case. (unit_names.js:45)

Energy Plant Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_energyplant, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Energy Plant"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Energy Plant Upgrade Tech increases the energy production of this basic economy structure by 25% but decreases its health by 50%."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_energyplant.js)

Energy Plant Upgrade Tech increases the.message: Energy Plant Upgrade Tech increases the energy production of this basic economy structure by 25% but decreases its health by 50%.
Energy Plant Upgrade Tech increases the.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Energy Plant Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. 'This basic economy structure' is the basic Energy Plant. The card multiplies its production.energy by 1.25 and its max_health by 0.5. Keep 25% and 50% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Energy Plant Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_energyplant.js:8)

Energy Storage.description: Unit name from the tech-card "Which Units?" tooltip on the galaxy map (gw_play): the tooltip lists every unit a tech card affects, one name per line. This is a stock Planetary Annihilation unit; use the game's existing translation of that unit's display name so the tooltip matches the in-game build bar. Noun, singular, title case. The same English text is also registered as a race-specific unit name (race descriptor unitNames) for the Bugs/Exiles races, where the race's own unit has the same name; keep the two identical. (unit_names.js:46, exiles.js:471)

Energy Storage Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_energystorage, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Energy Storage"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Energy Storage Upgrade Tech increases the amount of energy storage by 300%."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_energystorage.js)

Energy Storage Upgrade Tech increases th.message: Energy Storage Upgrade Tech increases the amount of energy storage by 300%.
Energy Storage Upgrade Tech increases th.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Energy Storage Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. The card multiplies the Energy Storage building's storage.energy by 4 (i.e. +300%). Keep 300% exactly. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Energy Storage Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_energystorage.js:8)

Epic.description: Galaxy size name, one of nine (Small, Medium, Large, Epic, Uber, Vast, Gigantic, Ridiculous, Marathon; the last four come from the Bigger Galactic War mod). Shown in the "Size:" row of the war-info panel on the galaxy map and as the third part of the auto-generated war name ("<Difficulty> - <N> Players - <Size> - <start card>"). Adjective used as a label, no punctuation; keep in step with the stock game's translation of the same size word where one exists. (setup.js:299)

Eradicate.description: Game modifier name listed under "Game Modifiers" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), one per line, and in the win-conditions line of the in-game HUD (live_game), where modifiers are joined with " | ". "Eradicate" is followed by a colon and the list of target types ("Eradicate: Commander, Colonel, Factory, Fabber"): the code appends the colon and list, so keep no punctuation in the string itself and make sure the word reads as a heading before a colon. Imperative verb used as a name; must match "ERADICATE" in the Game Modifiers tooltip. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:259, win_conditions_text.js:24)

Eradication Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card switches on the stock 'Eradicate' game modifier (a side loses only when all of its listed unit types are destroyed) in every battle of the war. Short title, noun phrase. Keep the root consistent with the game's existing translation of the 'Eradicate' game mode and with the description 'Eradication tech enables the eradicate game modifier in every system.' (gwaio_enable_eradication.js:9)

Eradication tech enables the eradicate g.message: Eradication tech enables the eradicate game modifier in every system.
Eradication tech enables the eradicate g.description: Body text of the tech card 'Eradication Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card turns on the stock 'Eradicate' win condition for every star system (battle) in the war. 'Eradicate' should use the game's existing translation of that game mode; 'system' means a star system on the galaxy map. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Eradication Tech' (English lower-cases 'tech' here; follow your locale's rule). (gwaio_enable_eradication.js:7)

Exiles.description: The name of the Exiles race, shown in the race picker, on the galaxy map and in unit tooltips wherever the faction is named. It is a proper noun: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean the way the game's own faction names are handled. (exiles.js:10)

FFA Chance.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Sits before a percentage dropdown; tooltip: "Chance of more than one faction being present in a system." FFA = free-for-all (keep the abbreviation or use the local gaming term). Title case (CSS up-cases it on screen), no trailing punctuation (the colon is outside the tag). (ai_settings.html:394)

FOUNDATION: air/navy.description:
One line of the faction tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start), shown beside the Faction dropdown. Lines read "FACTION NAME: preferred unit class", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is one of the game's enemy factions (a proper noun; render it as the game's own translation does, uppercased) and the word after the colon is the unit class that faction favours (vehicles, air/navy, bots, orbital, land), using the game's stock wording for that class. Keep the colon; no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoFactionTooltip) "air/navy" means aircraft and naval units; keep the slash or your locale's equivalent.

Fabber.description: Two uses. (1) AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel of the galaxy map (gw_play) and in the war-info panel. Adjective or noun used as a label, singular, no punctuation. A penchant word (Artillery, Fortress, Assault...) may be appended after it with a space, so keep it short. "Fabber" = a builder-focused style. (2) An eradication target listed after "Eradicate:" on the galaxy map and in the in-game HUD ("Eradicate: Commander, Colonel, Factory, Fabber"), meaning all enemy fabrication (builder) units must be destroyed. "Fabber" is the game's slang for a fabrication unit; use the base game's rendering of that word. Noun, singular. (gw_faction_0.js:46 and the other faction files, cluster_faction.js:32, section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:146, win_conditions_text.js:22)

Fabrication Aircraft.description: Unit name from the tech-card "Which Units?" tooltip on the galaxy map (gw_play): the tooltip lists every unit a tech card affects, one name per line. This is a stock Planetary Annihilation unit; use the game's existing translation of that unit's display name so the tooltip matches the in-game build bar. Noun, singular, title case. The same English text is also registered as a race-specific unit name (race descriptor unitNames) for the Bugs/Exiles races, where the race's own unit has the same name; keep the two identical. (unit_names.js:13, bugs.js:468)

Fabrication Aircraft Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_fabricationaircraft, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Fabrication Aircraft"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Fabrication Aircraft Upgrade Tech enables the building of advanced structures by the basic air fabricator."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_fabricationaircraft.js)

Fabrication Aircraft Upgrade Tech enable.message: Fabrication Aircraft Upgrade Tech enables the building of advanced structures by the basic air fabricator.
Fabrication Aircraft Upgrade Tech enable.description: Body text of the upgrade tech card 'Fabrication Aircraft Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal; the game appends a separate sentence about a new card slot after it. The card widens the basic air fabricator's buildable list to include advanced land structures (except factories) and unlocks the advanced starter structures. 'Advanced' is the game's word for tier 2, 'fabricator' for a construction unit. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Fabrication Aircraft Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_fabricationaircraft.js:10)

Fabrication Bot.description: Unit name from the tech-card "Which Units?" tooltip on the galaxy map (gw_play): the tooltip lists every unit a tech card affects, one name per line. IRON: you no longer turtle.description:
One line of the difficulty tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start): the "?" beside the Difficulty dropdown lists every difficulty level, one per line, as "LEVEL: who it suits". The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) "Turtle" is gaming slang: to play defensively and never attack.

'The solar drone' is the Icarus aircraft, which normally only generates energy; the card sets its production.metal to 2 (metal per second). Keep the number 2. 'Metal' is a game resource; use its standard translation. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Icarus Upgrade Tech'. (gwaio_upgrade_icarus.js:8)

If war is a commander's natural state, t.message: If war is a commander's natural state, then the purest expression of this is the Legionis Machina. It begs the question, though--what happens after they conquer this galaxy, if they do?
If war is a commander's natural state, t.description: Lore paragraph for the Legonis Machina faction, one of five shown at random as the description of a system they hold in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map. Stock flavour text; keep "--" as a dash and the final question mark. (Note the source spells the faction "Legionis Machina"; use the game's standard faction name.) (gw_faction_0.js:142)

Improved Commander Build Arm.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card makes the commander build 50% faster and use 50% less energy while building. Short title, noun phrase; 'build arm' is the game's term for a unit's construction tool. Note the name is singular ('Arm') while the description says 'Build Arms'; keep them recognisably the same card and parallel with 'Improved Fabricator Build Arms'. (gwc_bld_efficiency_cdr.js:10)

Improved Commander Build Arms increase b.message: Improved Commander Build Arms increase build speed of all Commanders' build arms by 50% and reduces energy usage by 50%.
Improved Commander Build Arms increase b.description: Body text of the tech card 'Improved Commander Build Arm', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies the commander build arm's construction_demand.metal by 1.5 (that is how the game expresses build speed) and its construction_demand.energy by 0.5. 'Commanders'' is a plural possessive. Keep both 50% figures. The opening words should echo the translated card name 'Improved Commander Build Arm'. (gwc_bld_efficiency_cdr.js:8)

Improved Energy Weapons.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card cuts the energy that energy-based weapons (lasers and similar) drain when firing by 75%. Short title, noun phrase, plural 'Weapons'; 'Improved' is an adjective. Must match the opening words of its description 'Improved Energy Weapons tech reduces energy costs...'. (gwc_energy_efficiency_weapons.js:11)

Improved Energy Weapons tech reduces ene.message: Improved Energy Weapons tech reduces energy costs for energy based weapons by 75%
Improved Energy Weapons tech reduces ene.description: Body text of the tech card 'Improved Energy Weapons', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies the per-shot energy demand of every energy-based weapon by 0.25. Keep 75% exactly; no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Improved Energy Weapons' (English adds a lower-case 'tech' after the name; follow your locale's rule). (gwc_energy_efficiency_weapons.js:9)

Improved Fabricator Build Arms.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card makes every fabricator and factory (but not the commander) build 50% faster and use 50% less energy while building. Short title, noun phrase, plural 'Arms'; 'build arm' is the game's term for a unit's construction tool. Keep parallel with 'Improved Commander Build Arm'. Must match the opening words of its description. (gwc_bld_efficiency_fabs.js:17)

Improved Fabricator Build Arms increase.message: Improved Fabricator Build Arms increase the build speed of all fabricator and factory build arms by 50% and reduces energy usage by 50%.
Improved Fabricator Build Arms increase.description: Body text of the tech card 'Improved Fabricator Build Arms', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies construction_demand.metal of every fabricator and factory build arm by 1.5 (that is how the game expresses build speed) and construction_demand.energy by 0.5; the commander's own arm is covered by a separate card. Keep both 50% figures. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Improved Fabricator Build Arms'. (gwc_bld_efficiency_fabs.js:15)

Improved Intelligence Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal. The card cuts the energy drain of intelligence structures (radar, jammers and similar) by 75%. Short title, noun phrase; 'Intelligence' means military intel/reconnaissance, not cleverness. Must match the opening words of its description. (gwc_energy_efficiency_intel.js:11)

Improved Intelligence Tech reduces energ.message: Improved Intelligence Tech reduces energy costs for intelligence structures by 75%
Improved Intelligence Tech reduces energ.description: Body text of the tech card 'Improved Intelligence Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip and the tech deal. The card multiplies consumption.energy of every intelligence (radar, jammer, orbital radar) structure by 0.25. 'Intelligence' means military intel/reconnaissance. Keep 75% exactly; no full stop at the end in English. The opening words must match the translated card name 'Improved Intelligence Tech'. (gwc_energy_efficiency_intel.js:9)

In researching ancient progenitor artifa.message: In researching ancient progenitor artifacts and data caches, Nemicus and his followers discovered references to The Great Machine. Supposedly, The Great Machine was what built and directed the commanders long ago. If any answers about the origins and purpose of the commanders were to be found, The Great Machine seemed like the best place to start.
In researching ancient progenitor artifa.description: Lore paragraph for the Foundation faction, one of five shown at random as the description of a system they hold in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map. Stock flavour text; Nemicus is a commander name, "The Great Machine" and "progenitor" are lore terms; keep the final full stop. (gw_faction_1.js:141)

Incompatible Mods.description: Sub-heading in the war-info panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), shown only when the player has client mods enabled that conflict with GWO; the list of those mods follows. Noun phrase, plural, title case, no punctuation; "Mods" = the modifications (things), not an action. (gwo_panel.html:117)

Increases the speed of all Titans by 20%.message: Increases the speed of all Titans by 20%.
Increases the speed of all Titans by 20%.description: Body text of a tech card. Shown in the Data Bank card list, in the card tooltip on the galaxy map, and in the tech deal offered after a battle. This is the description of the card 'Titan Engine Tech': it multiplies the movement speed of every mobile Titan unit by 1.2. Keep '20%' exactly. 'Titans' is the game's own class name for the largest units (Atlas, Ares, Zeus, Helios, Omega, Kaiju, Narwhal) and should use the game's existing translation for that term. (gwaio_speed_titans.js:7)

Infernodier.description: Penchant name: a one-word style bias an AI Commander can be given when the war's AI is set to PENCHANT. On the galaxy map it is appended after the personality trait in the "Personality:" row, joined with a space (e.g. "Aggressive Artillery"), so it must read as a noun/adjective that can follow a trait word; word order of that pairing cannot be changed. Singular, no punctuation. "Infernodier" is a coined name (Inferno + Grenadier: favours the Inferno flamethrower bot and grenadier-type bots); treat as an invented proper-ish noun, transliterate or coin an equivalent. (ai.js:195)

Intelligence Fabrication Tech.description: Name of a tech card; a short title (noun phrase). LAND ANYWHERE CHANCE:.description: Label on the AI Settings panel on the war setup screen (gw_start), which appears when the Custom difficulty is chosen. Upper-case noun phrase; keep the trailing colon; "Land Anywhere" must match the game modifier name of that name. (ai_settings.html:440)

LAND ANYWHERE: players can start anywher.message: LAND ANYWHERE: players can start anywhere on viable starting planets.
LAND ANYWHERE: players can start anywher.description:
One line of the Game Modifiers tooltip on the galaxy map's system intelligence panel (gw_play). Each line is "MODIFIER NAME: what it does", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is a game modifier that must match the same modifier's name elsewhere (the Game Modifiers list and the in-battle win-conditions line use the title-case form: Bounties, Land Anywhere, Sudden Death, Eradicate). Keep the colon and the full stop; no line break in the string. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js, gwoGameModifiersTooltip)

LEGONIS MACHINA: vehicles.description:
One line of the faction tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start), shown beside the Faction dropdown. Lines read "FACTION NAME: preferred unit class", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is one of the game's enemy factions (a proper noun; render it as the game's own translation does, uppercased) and the word after the colon is the unit class that faction favours (vehicles, air/navy, bots, orbital, land), using the game's stock wording for that class. Keep the colon; no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoFactionTooltip)

LOCKED.description: Value in the "Player Slots:" row of the co-op table in the war-info panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), meaning no further players may join (the alternative is "Unlocked"). Reuses the base game's upper-case "LOCKED" entry (CSS sentence-cases it on screen), so match that translation. Adjective/past participle, no punctuation. (gwo_panel.js:246)

Land Anywhere.description: Game modifier name listed under "Game Modifiers" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map (gw_play), one per line, and in the win-conditions line of the in-game HUD (live_game), where modifiers are joined with " | ". "Land Anywhere" = players may choose any starting position instead of fixed spawn zones. Verb phrase used as a name, title case, no punctuation; must match "LAND ANYWHERE" in the Game Modifiers tooltip and the "LAND ANYWHERE CHANCE:" label. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:247)

Land Anywhere Tech.description: Name of a tech card; a short title (noun phrase). Shown in the Data Bank card list, in the card tooltip on the galaxy map, and in the tech deal offered after a battle. The card turns on the game's 'Land Anywhere' option for every battle, so the player may drop their commander anywhere on the planet rather than in a fixed landing zone. 'Land Anywhere' is the name of an existing game lobby setting; reuse the game's translation of that setting. 'Land' is the verb (to land a commander), not the noun. Must agree with the card body 'Land Anywhere tech enables the land anywhere game modifier in every system.'. (gwaio_enable_landanywhere.js:9)

Land Anywhere tech enables the land anyw.message: Land Anywhere tech enables the land anywhere game modifier in every system.
Land Anywhere tech enables the land anyw.description: Body text of a tech card. Shown in the Data Bank card list, in the card tooltip on the galaxy map, and in the tech deal offered after a battle. The card enables the stock 'Land Anywhere' lobby option in every battle of the war, letting commanders land at any point on a planet. 'land anywhere game modifier' refers to that lobby setting; reuse the game's translation of it. 'system' means a star system on the galaxy map. The opening 'Land Anywhere tech' should match the card name 'Land Anywhere Tech' (the lowercase 'tech' is a source inconsistency, not a different term). (gwaio_enable_landanywhere.js:7)

Land Mine.description: Unit name from the tech-card "Which Units?" tooltip on the galaxy map (gw_play): the tooltip lists every unit a tech card affects, one name per line. This is a stock Planetary Annihilation unit; use the game's existing translation of that unit's display name so the tooltip matches the in-game build bar. Noun, singular, title case. Original.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map when a star is selected (and in the same slot on the GWO panel for Sub Commanders). Adjective used as a label: the Commander plays with the base game's original, unmodified AI personality. Same string in all four factions. (gw_faction_0.js:97)

Osiris has always lead a solitary existe.message: Osiris has always lead a solitary existence. He was always more interested in the parts of his fellow commanders than the commanders themselves. With every battle won he would take the best pieces left of the broken adversary and integrate them into his form. Osiris is considered one of the most dangerous forces in the galaxy.
Osiris has always lead a solitary existe.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Revenants faction; Osiris is a proper name. (gw_faction_3.js:136)

Osiris holds no interest in ruling, and.message: Osiris holds no interest in ruling, and instead serves more as an exemplar, whether he cares to or not. Therefore, it falls to a small council of older Seekers to direct the affairs of The Revenants at large--primarily making sure that they're fighting the other factions instead of amongst themselves.
Osiris holds no interest in ruling, and.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Osiris often considered the most dangero.message: Osiris often considered the most dangerous commander in all the galaxy for the amount of annihilations he is credited with. A force of war equal to any army, high command of any faction takes his movements into consideration when deploying forces.
Osiris often considered the most dangero.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Revenants faction; Osiris is a proper name. The English omits "is" after Osiris; translate the intended meaning. (gw_faction_3.js:140)

Osmech.description: Name of Osmech, a unit expansion mod. Shown on the war panel when the mod was enabled at war creation and is off now. A proper noun: keep untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales; transliterate in ja/ko as PA's legion.json does.

PENCHANT: increased personality.description:
One line of the introduction text in the AI picker dialog on the war setup screen (gw_start), which lets the player choose which AI runs each race. Lines read "AI NAME: what it offers", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is an AI: TITANS is the base game's AI, QUELLER and PENCHANT are AI mods; these are proper nouns and stay as written. Keep the colon; no line break in the string. (ai_picker.js, gwoAiModalIntro) "Personality" means the AI's play styles are more distinct from one another.

PERSONALITY MODIFIERS:.description: Label on the AI Settings dialog opened from the war setup screen (Galactic War start). Uppercase row label, keep the trailing colon; precedes a drop-down of tweaks to the AI's personality. Must agree with its tooltip "Tweaks to how the AI plays." (ai_settings.html:363)

PLATINUM: one enemy is no challenge.message: PLATINUM: one enemy is no challenge
PLATINUM: one enemy is no challenge.description:
One line of the difficulty tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start): the "?" beside the Difficulty dropdown lists every difficulty level, one per line, as "LEVEL: who it suits". The upper-case word before the colon is the difficulty level's name as it appears in the dropdown; keep it as the game's own translation of that level renders it (uppercased) and keep the colon. The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip)

PLAYER.description: The singular unit word after a count on the "Scaling For:" row of the Galactic War Overhaul panel on the galaxy map: "1 PLAYER" (CSS then lowercases it to "1 Player"). Noun, singular; the plural form is the separate string "Players". Match the base game's translation of PLAYER. (gwo_panel.js:30)

POV Camera.description: Label of an item on the in-battle menu (opened from the menu button during a Galactic War battle). The base game ships this same menu item, so match the base-game wording. Toggles the point-of-view camera. (menu.js:63)

Paratrooper Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout (a 'Commander' card chosen when a war begins). Shown as the loadout's title in the loadout picker at war start and in the Data Bank; the second site uses the same string as the caption of the locked placeholder shown before the loadout is unlocked. In this loadout the player has no basic land or air factories and instead fires units from Lobs and Unit Cannons, hence 'paratrooper' (troops dropped from above). 'Paratrooper' is a noun used as a modifier; 'Commander' is the player's hero unit and should use the game's existing translation. Follow the same '<Modifier> Commander' structure as 'Lucky Commander' and 'Nomad Commander'. (gwaio_start_paratrooper.js:88)

Part of the doctrine of The Synchronous.message: Part of the doctrine of The Synchronous is favoring the efficiency of 'mechanical purity.' To them, the galaxy as a whole is a great machine, and anything that keeps it from running at peak efficiency must be corrected or removed. This happens to often mean any and all organic life and unsynchronized commanders.
Part of the doctrine of The Synchronous.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. First sentence of the card body; the game follows it with a space and the separate string 'Every unit can shoot while being transported.', so make the two read as one paragraph. Planetary Excavation Commander.description: Name of a starting loadout (a 'Commander' card chosen when a war begins). Used as the in-game unit name (build bar, selection panel, unit tooltip) of the structure that the card 'Planetary Radar Tech' unlocks, and in the mod's unit-name table used for card and Data Bank text. It is an advanced radar structure whose radar covers the whole planet. Keep it identical with the wording used inside 'Planetary Radar Tech', 'Planetary Radar Upgrade Tech' and the description 'Planetary Radar - Detects enemy land, sea, and air units across the planet.'. (gwaio_enable_planetaryradar.js:32; unit_names.js:99)

Planetary Radar - Detects enemy land, se.message: Planetary Radar - Detects enemy land, sea, and air units across the planet.

It states that the structure's radar reveals every enemy land, sea and air unit on the planet. Keep the 'Name - Description' layout with the hyphen, matching the game's stock unit descriptions, and keep 'Planetary Radar' identical to the unit name string. (gwaio_enable_planetaryradar.js:34)

Planetary Radar Tech.description: Name of a tech card; a short title (noun phrase). Shown in the Data Bank card list, in the card tooltip on the galaxy map, and in the tech deal offered after a battle. The card unlocks the Planetary Radar, a structure whose radar covers the whole planet. 'Planetary Radar' must be identical to the unit name string 'Planetary Radar'. Must agree with the card body 'Enables the building of the Planetary Radar which provides complete planetary radar coverage.'. (gwaio_enable_planetaryradar.js:11)

Planetary Radar Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_planetaryradar, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. (gwaio_upgrade_planetaryradar.js)

Planetary Radar Upgrade Tech increases t.message: Planetary Radar Upgrade Tech increases the vision of the planetary radar to match its radar.
Planetary Radar Upgrade Tech increases t.description: Body text of a tech card. Shown in the Data Bank card list, in the card tooltip on the galaxy map, and in the tech deal offered after a battle. The card multiplies the Planetary Radar structure's sight radius so it sees (not merely detects on radar) everything on the planet. 'vision' means direct line of sight; 'radar' means the radar-blip detection range. The opening 'Planetary Radar Upgrade Tech' must match the card name. Platinum.description: Name of a Galactic War difficulty level (the ninth of ten: Beginner, Casual, Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Uber, Custom). Shown in the difficulty drop-down on the war setup screen, in the generated war name, in the co-op lobby title and on the "Difficulty:" row of the GWO panel. Platoon.description: Penchant name: a one-word label for the Penchant AI's extra specialisation, shown after the personality trait in the "Personality:" line of the Planetary Intelligence panel, e.g. "Rush Minelayer". The two words are joined by a space in code, so word order cannot be changed; choose a form that reads naturally after the trait. Noun: an AI that fights in platoons (grouped units). (ai.js:243)

Player Guide.description: Label of an item on the in-battle menu (opened from the menu button during a Galactic War battle). The base game ships this same menu item, so match the base-game wording. Opens the in-game player guide. (menu.js:55)

Player Slots:.description: Row label on the Galactic War Overhaul info panel shown on the galaxy map (a value follows on the same row). In the Co-Op Settings section; followed by "Locked" or "Unlocked" (whether more players may join). Noun, plural; keep the trailing colon. (gwo_panel.html:98)

Players.description: Plural noun after a count. Two uses: the war name generated on the war setup screen, e.g. "Gold 2 Players Small"; and the "Scaling For:" row of the GWO panel on the galaxy map, e.g. "2 Players" (only when the count is above one; "PLAYER" is used for one). The number always precedes the word. Match the base game's "Players". (gwo_panel.js:30)

Players returned.description: Status line on the post-battle waiting panel in a co-op war, assembled as "Players returned: 2 / 3" (returned count / expected count). Short phrase, no trailing punctuation (the colon is added in code). (systems.js:358)

Prefers air and navy..description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the faction name (Foundation) heading in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map; says which unit types that faction's AI favours. Sentence fragment with a full stop; keep it. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:67)

Prefers bots and vehicles; applies tech.message: Prefers bots and vehicles; applies tech to structures.

Prefers bots..description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the Synchronous faction heading in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map; "bots" are the bot unit class. Keep the full stop. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:68)

Prefers orbital..description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the Revenants faction heading in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map; "orbital" means orbital units. Keep the full stop. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:69)

Prefers vehicles..description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the Legonis Machina faction heading in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map. Keep the full stop. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:66)

Preparing for battle.description: Title of the launch progress panel shown after pressing Fight on the galaxy map while the battle is being prepared; the stage lines ("Mounting game files" etc.) appear beneath it. The leading card name must match the translation of the card name 'Single Laser Defense Tower Upgrade Tech' exactly. Some commanders fight because it's all t.message: Some commanders fight because it's all they know, while others seek answers to their origins. Conflicts in motivation and creed drive the commanders into a war that is poised to ravage the galaxy for centuries.
Some commanders fight because it's all t.description: Lore text: the description shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map for a neutral system, beneath the matching lore title. Full paragraph. Pairs with the title "Galactic War". (lore.js:13)

Space Excavation Commander.description: Name of a starting commander loadout (a start card). Shown as the loadout's title in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War, and in the Data Bank; the same string is also shown as the placeholder label of that loadout while it is still locked (unearned), so it must read well both as a title and as a locked-entry label. This loadout modifies the Jig (orbital mining platform) so it can be built anywhere, cheaper but less productive, gives orbital fabbers all basic structures, and forbids ordinary metal extractors, power plants and the Omega battleship. Must agree with the wording of its description that begins 'Modifies Jigs to allow building them anywhere...'. 'Commander' is the game's standard term for the player's commander unit and must use the same word as every other '... Commander' loadout name. Used both as the card name (line 105) and as the locked-loadout hint label (line 112). (nem_start_deepspace.js:105)
