Sub Commander Fabber Tech increases the.message: Sub Commander Fabber Tech increases the number of fabbers each Sub Commander may use by 50%.
Sub Commander Fabber Tech increases the.description: Description of the upgrade tech card 'Sub Commander Fabber Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The allied Sub Commander AI's fabricator cap is multiplied by 1.5. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Sub Commander Fabber Tech' exactly; 'fabbers' is the game's short word for fabrication units. Keep '50%' exactly. (gwaio_upgrade_subcommander_fabber.js:8)

Sub Commander Tactics Tech.description: Name of an upgrade tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card switches the allied Sub Commander AIs to a smarter AI configuration for scouting, fighting, expanding and retreating. Must agree with its description 'Sub Commander Tactics Tech allows Sub Commanders to make smarter decisions...'. Title-style noun phrase; 'Tactics' is a noun. (gwaio_upgrade_subcommander_tactics.js:5)

Sub Commander Tactics Tech allows Sub Co.message: Sub Commander Tactics Tech allows Sub Commanders to make smarter decisions when scouting, fighting, expanding, and escaping danger.
Sub Commander Tactics Tech allows Sub Co.description: Description of the upgrade tech card 'Sub Commander Tactics Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The allied Sub Commander AIs get improved decision-making in those four areas. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Sub Commander Tactics Tech' exactly; 'Sub Commanders' is plural of the game's term for allied AI commanders. (gwaio_upgrade_subcommander_tactics.js:7)

Sudden Death.description: Name of a game modifier: any Commander death on a team kills the whole team. Listed under "Game Modifiers" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map and in the win-conditions text shown during a battle. Noun phrase, title case; must match the wording inside "SUDDEN DEATH CHANCE:" and the game modifiers tooltip. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:253)

Sudden Death Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card turns on the game's 'Sudden Death' lobby modifier (a commander's death eliminates that player immediately) for every battle in the war. 'Sudden Death' is the base game's own name for that game option and must use the same translation as the stock lobby setting. Must agree with its description 'Sudden Death tech enables the sudden death game modifier in every system.' Title-style noun phrase. (gwaio_enable_suddendeath.js:10)

Sudden Death tech enables the sudden dea.message: Sudden Death tech enables the sudden death game modifier in every system.
Sudden Death tech enables the sudden dea.description: Description of the tech card 'Sudden Death Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. Every battle is set up with the stock 'Sudden Death' game option on. The leading card name should match the translation of 'Sudden Death Tech' (the source has lower-case 'tech' and 'sudden death' here; matching the card name's casing is fine). 'System' means a star system on the galaxy map, i.e. every battle. (gwaio_enable_suddendeath.js:8)

Super Weapon Fabrication Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card cuts the metal cost of nuclear missiles, Halley engines and metal-planet control modules by 75%. Must agree with its description 'Super Weapon Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all nuclear missiles, Halley Rockets, and metal planet control modules by 75%...'. Title-style noun phrase, parallel to 'Vehicle Fabrication Tech' etc. ('Fabrication' = building/construction). (gwc_cost_super_weapons.js:12)

Super Weapon Fabrication Tech reduces me.message: Super Weapon Fabrication Tech reduces metal build costs of all nuclear missiles, Halley Rockets, and metal planet control modules by 75%. Tech to build super weapons is required.
Super Weapon Fabrication Tech reduces me.description: Description of the tech card 'Super Weapon Fabrication Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. Metal build cost of nukes, the Halley planet-moving engine and the metal-planet (Annihilaser) control module is multiplied by 0.25. The last sentence warns that the card only matters if the player already has the blueprints for those super weapons. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Super Weapon Fabrication Tech' exactly; 'Halley' is the game's own name for the planet engine and stays as the game's unit tables have it. Keep '75%' exactly. (gwc_cost_super_weapons.js:10)

Surface Area:.description: Row label in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map, followed by the system's total surface area with "km²" appended. Noun; keep the trailing colon. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.html:9)

Surrender.description: Label of an item on the in-battle menu (opened from the menu button during a Galactic War battle). The base game ships this same menu item, so match the base-game wording. Verb (imperative); the surrender item, shown instead of "Abandon War" when Hardcore is off. Match the base game's Surrender. (menu.js:33)

Swarm.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map when a star is selected (and in the same slot on the GWO panel for Sub Commanders). Noun/verb used as a label: this Commander masses many cheap units. Same string in all factions and the Cluster. (gw_faction_0.js:117)

Swarm Commander.description: Name of a starting commander loadout (a start card). Shown as the loadout's title in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War, and in the Data Bank; the same string is also shown as the placeholder label of that loadout while it is still locked (unearned), so it must read well both as a title and as a locked-entry label. This loadout makes all units twice as fast and 30% cheaper but halves their damage. Must agree with its description 'This Commander likes to raid and has modified its blueprints to that end...'. 'Swarm' evokes many cheap fast units; 'Commander' must use the same word as every other '... Commander' loadout name. Used both as the card name (line 40) and as the locked-loadout hint label (line 47). (tgw_start_speed.js:40)

System Lore.description: Label of the "System Lore" switch in the Game Options dialog on the war setup screen: shows the original pre-release Galactic War lore text in the star detail card. Title case noun phrase. Must agree with its tooltip. (difficulty_options.html:156)

System Scaling.description: Label of the "System Scaling" switch in the Game Options dialog on the war setup screen: system size grows with distance into the galaxy. Title case noun phrase. Its lowercase twin "System scaling" is the same option on the GWO panel; translate both the same apart from casing. Must agree with its tooltip "System size determined by distance into the galaxy." (difficulty_options.html:85)

System scaling.description: Entry in the "Options:" list on the GWO panel on the galaxy map when the System Scaling game option is on. Sentence-case twin of "System Scaling"; translate identically apart from casing. (gwo_panel.js:123)

System size determined by distance into.message: System size determined by distance into the galaxy.
System size determined by distance into.description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the "System Scaling" switch in the Game Options dialog on the war setup screen. Sentence fragment with a full stop; keep it. (difficulty_options.html:88)

TARGET SELECTION:.description: Label on the AI Settings dialog opened from the war setup screen (Galactic War start). Uppercase row label, keep the trailing colon; how well the AI chooses whom to attack. Must agree with its tooltip "How well the AI picks who to attack." (ai_settings.html:307)

TECH SYSTEM:.description: Label on the AI Settings dialog opened from the war setup screen (Galactic War start). Uppercase row label, keep the trailing colon; the number of systems into the galaxy after which enemy AIs gain tech bonuses. Must agree with its tooltip "Number of systems until AI tech appears." (ai_settings.html:122)

TECHS.description: Label of the tech card deck drop-down on the war setup screen ("TECHS:" - the colon sits outside the tag, do not add one), choosing between the Basic and Galactic War Overhaul card decks. Uppercase plural noun, short for technologies (tech cards). The base game ships the same string in gw_play; match it. (cards_dropdown.html:2)

TITANS: base game AI.description:
One line of the introduction text in the AI picker dialog on the war setup screen (gw_start), which lets the player choose which AI runs each race. Lines read "AI NAME: what it offers", joined with
by the code. The upper-case name before the colon is an AI: TITANS is the base game's AI, QUELLER and PENCHANT are AI mods; these are proper nouns and stay as written. Keep the colon; no line break in the string. (ai_picker.js, gwoAiModalIntro)

Tactical.description: Penchant name: a one-word label for the Penchant AI's extra specialisation, shown after the personality trait in the "Personality:" line of the Planetary Intelligence panel, e.g. "Rush Minelayer". The two words are joined by a space in code, so word order cannot be changed; choose a form that reads naturally after the trait. Adjective used as a label: an AI that favours tactical (mid-range missile) units. (ai.js:233)

Tactical Nuke - Small nuke with low dama.message: Tactical Nuke - Small nuke with low damage and small blast radius.
Tactical Nuke - Small nuke with low dama.description: In-game unit description (the text shown in the unit's hover card / build tooltip during a battle) that the Tactical Nuke Commander loadout writes over the nuclear missile's normal description. Format is 'Unit name - one-line summary'; keep the ' - ' separator. 'Tactical Nuke' is the modified missile's display name and must match the name used in the loadout name 'Tactical Nuke Commander' and in the launcher blurb 'Tactical Nuke Launcher - ...'. 'Nuke' is the game's short word for a nuclear missile. (nem_start_nuke.js:48)

Tactical Nuke Commander.description: Name of a starting commander loadout (a start card). Shown as the loadout's title in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War, and in the Data Bank; the same string is also shown as the placeholder label of that loadout while it is still locked (unearned), so it must read well both as a title and as a locked-entry label. This loadout replaces normal nukes with very cheap, very weak 'tactical' nukes and gives up most advanced defences. Must agree with its description 'Replaces conventional nukes with a new low-cost/low-yield variant...' and with the unit blurbs 'Tactical Nuke Launcher - ...' and 'Tactical Nuke - ...'. 'Nuke' is the game's short word for a nuclear missile; 'Commander' must use the same word as every other '... Commander' loadout name. Used both as the card name (line 69) and as the locked-loadout hint label (line 76). (nem_start_nuke.js:69)

Tactical Nuke Launcher - Constructs low-.message: Tactical Nuke Launcher - Constructs low-cost/low-yield interplanetary tactical nukes.
Tactical Nuke Launcher - Constructs low-.description: In-game unit description (the text shown in the structure's hover card / build tooltip during a battle) that the Tactical Nuke Commander loadout writes over the Nuke Launcher's normal description. Format is 'Unit name - one-line summary'; keep the ' - ' separator. 'Tactical Nuke Launcher' must use the same words as 'Tactical Nuke' in the sibling missile blurb plus the game's own word for the Nuke Launcher structure. 'Low-cost/low-yield' means cheap and weak; 'interplanetary' means it can hit other planets. (nem_start_nuke.js:33)

Tech:.description: Row label on the Galactic War Overhaul info panel shown on the galaxy map (a value follows on the same row). In the Co-Op Settings section; followed by "Shared" or "Separate" (whether players share tech cards). Noun, short for technology; keep the trailing colon. (gwo_panel.html:94)

Technologist.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map when a star is selected (and in the same slot on the GWO panel for Sub Commanders). Noun: this Commander rushes advanced technology. Same string in all factions and the Cluster. (gw_faction_0.js:65)

Teleporter.description: Unit display name. Listed in the "Which Units?" tooltip on a tech card (galaxy map, card offer and inventory panels) to say which units the card affects. Noun, singular. Use the game's own name for this unit exactly as it appears in the base game's unit list so the tooltip matches the in-game unit; do not invent a new name. Base-game structure name; the second site is the Exiles race's own unit table for the same purpose and should match. (unit_names.js:89)

Teleporter Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_teleporter, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Teleporter"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Teleporter Upgrade Tech removes all energy consumption and efficiency requirements from the interplanetary teleporter and makes it invisible to radar."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_teleporter.js)

Teleporter Upgrade Tech removes all ener.message: Teleporter Upgrade Tech removes all energy consumption and efficiency requirements from the interplanetary teleporter and makes it invisible to radar.
Teleporter Upgrade Tech removes all ener.description: Description of the upgrade tech card 'Teleporter Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card upgrades the Teleporter structure: its energy demand and energy-efficiency requirement are set to zero and it is flagged to ignore radar detection. The leading card name must match the translation of the card name 'Teleporter Upgrade Tech' exactly. Rendered as body text under the card name; the game appends a second paragraph about a new technology slot, so end the sentence with the same punctuation as the source. 'Efficiency' is the game's term for the economy efficiency percentage. (gwaio_upgrade_teleporter.js:8)

Temperature:.description: Label in the per-planet tooltip on the planet icons of the star detail card on the galaxy map, followed by a space and a number. Noun; keep the trailing colon. Agrees with "Radius:" and "Water Height:". (systems.js:203)

Terminal Commander.description: Name of a starting commander loadout (a start card). Shown as the loadout's title in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War, and in the Data Bank; the same string is also shown as the placeholder label of that loadout while it is still locked (unearned), so it must read well both as a title and as a locked-entry label. This loadout makes every unit slowly lose health over time (the commander fastest) in exchange for double damage and speed and half cost. 'Terminal' is in the medical sense (terminally ill, dying), which the description 'You're dying, but you have one last war left in you...' spells out; pick a word that keeps that meaning. 'Commander' must use the same word as every other '... Commander' loadout name. Used both as the card name (line 52) and as the locked-loadout hint label (line 65). (gwaio_start_terminal.js:52)

The Air Commander loadout contains basic.message: The Air Commander loadout contains basic air factories.
The Air Commander loadout contains basic.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Air Commander loadout: the player starts with the basic air factory and its units. 'Air Commander' must match the translation of the loadout name 'Air Commander'; 'loadout' is the game's word for a starting set of blueprints. (gwc_start_air.js:23)

The Artillery Commander loadout contains.message: The Artillery Commander loadout contains all artillery units and reduces costs of those structures by 75%. It also enables the Commander to build radar, double barreled turrets and basic artillery turrets.
The Artillery Commander loadout contains.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Artillery Commander loadout: all artillery structures at 25% of their normal metal cost, plus the commander itself can build radar, the double-barrelled laser tower and the basic artillery turret. 'Artillery Commander' must match the translation of the loadout name 'Artillery Commander'. Keep '75%' exactly; 'double barreled turrets' describes the Laser Defense Tower, and 'basic artillery turrets' the Pelter, so use the game's normal terms rather than inventing names. (gwc_start_artillery.js:47)

The Assault Commander loadout contains a.message: The Assault Commander loadout contains all basic factories and units but no basic defenses.
The Assault Commander loadout contains a.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Assault Commander loadout: every basic factory (bot, vehicle, air, naval) and their units, but none of the basic defence structures. 'Assault Commander' must match the translation of the loadout name 'Assault Commander'. (gwc_start_allfactory.js:42)

The Bionic Augmentation Commander Of Neu.message: The Bionic Augmentation Commander Of Neutralizing loadout contains one data bank but increases the Commander's fire rate by 100%, decreases Uber Cannon energy usage by 75%, increases health by 200%, and increases speed by 400%.
The Bionic Augmentation Commander Of Neu.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the 'Bionic Augmentation Commander Of Neutralizing' loadout (a joke name whose initials spell BACON): a heavily buffed commander unit with only one tech slot. The loadout name must be reproduced exactly as translated for the card name 'Bionic Augmentation Commander Of Neutralizing'. 'Data bank' is the game's term for a tech card slot; 'Uber Cannon' is the commander's special weapon and stays as the game's own tables have it. Keep '100%', '75%', '200%' and '400%' exactly. (gwc_start_combatcdr.js:40)

The Bot Commander loadout contains basic.message: The Bot Commander loadout contains basic bot factories.
The Bot Commander loadout contains basic.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Bot Commander loadout: the player starts with the basic bot factory and its units. 'Bot Commander' must match the translation of the loadout name 'Bot Commander'; 'bot' is the game's own word for its walking robot units. (gwc_start_bot.js:23)

The Commander can mass teleport itself a.message: The Commander can mass teleport itself and all units within weapons range to anywhere in the system, but they are highly vulnerable to attack afterwards.
The Commander can mass teleport itself a.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Warp Commander loadout: the commander unit gains a mass-teleport order (radius 100, a 30-second phasing period during which the teleported units have 1% health, a large energy cost) that moves it and nearby mobile units anywhere in the star system. Must agree with the loadout name 'Warp Commander'. 'Commander' is the commander unit; 'system' means the star system (all its planets). (gwaio_start_warp.js:43)

The Commanders.description: Title of a lore entry shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map for a neutral system, above its description ("The commanders have slumbered for millions of years..."). Noun phrase with article, plural. (lore.js:16)

The General Commander loadout contains v.message: The General Commander loadout contains very limited mobile forces and only two data banks. However, the loadout comes with two Sub Commanders that accompany you into each battle.
The General Commander loadout contains v.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the General Commander loadout ('General' as in the military rank): few units and only two tech slots, but two allied AI Sub Commanders fight alongside the player in every battle. 'General Commander' must match the translation of the loadout name 'General Commander'; 'data banks' is the game's term for tech card slots; 'Sub Commanders' must use the same translation as the 'Sub Commander' card. (gwc_start_subcdr.js:42)

The Legion.description: Title of a lore entry shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map for a neutral system, above its description ("Scattered references point to the Progenitors..."). "Legion" is the proper name of the Legion faction/race; keep the name as the Legion mod does. (lore.js:26)

The Legionis Machina can be considered a.message: The Legionis Machina can be considered a cult of personality, in that their purpose is void without Invictus. This is likely where their bitter hatred of The Synchronous comes from, as they view Metrarch as a false idol of sorts.
The Legionis Machina can be considered a.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Legonis Machina faction; Legionis Machina, Invictus, The Synchronous and Metrarch are proper names. (gw_faction_0.js:143)

The Legionis Machina has claimed confirm.message: The Legionis Machina has claimed confirmed kills of Metrarch the Machinist on several occasions. While these claims could easily be fabricated, it is also possible that Metrarch is not in fact a single commander, but rather an idea--an avatar of the Whole itself that manifests where necessary to protect Synchronous interests.
The Legionis Machina has claimed confirm.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Synchronous faction; Legionis Machina, Metrarch the Machinist, the Whole and Synchronous are proper names. The double hyphen is a dash. (gw_faction_2.js:137)

The Lucky Commander is offered four card.message: The Lucky Commander is offered four cards instead of three at every planet.
The Lucky Commander is offered four card.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Lucky Commander loadout: its only effect is that the tech deal after each battle offers 4 cards instead of the usual 3. 'Lucky Commander' must match the translation of the loadout name 'Lucky Commander'. 'Cards' are the tech cards of the Galactic War; keep the numbers four and three. (gwaio_start_lucky.js:22)

The Machine Liberation Army.description: Title of a lore entry shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map for a neutral system, above its description ("Buried deep within the data banks..."). Proper name of the MLA, the base game's default race; keep consistent with how "MLA" is expanded elsewhere. (lore.js:21)

The Naval Commander loadout contains all.message: The Naval Commander loadout contains all naval factories. Increases the amount of water and lava on eligible planets.
The Naval Commander loadout contains all.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Naval Commander loadout: all naval factories and ships, and battle planets are generated with more sea (or lava) so there is somewhere to sail. The loadout name is assembled at runtime from the two separate strings 'Naval' and 'Commander', so the words 'Naval Commander' here must match how those two strings read when joined. (gwaio_start_naval.js:23)

The Orbital Commander loadout contains a.message: The Orbital Commander loadout contains all orbital units and factories.
The Orbital Commander loadout contains a.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Orbital Commander loadout: the orbital launcher, orbital factory and every orbital unit. 'Orbital Commander' must match the translation of the loadout name 'Orbital Commander'; 'orbital' is the game's own term for its space layer. (gwc_start_orbital.js:23)

The Progenitors.description: Title of a lore entry shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map for a neutral system, above its description ("What little is clear is that the galaxy was once inhabited..."). Proper name of the vanished civilisation; must match "Progenitors" inside the lore texts. (lore.js:6)

The Revenants are unique in that their m.message: The Revenants are unique in that their motivations are individual rather than collective. Each Seeker follows in the example of their legendary Osiris--they seek battle to become stronger through their fallen enemies, and to create more Revenants.
The Revenants are unique in that their m.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Revenants faction; Revenants, Seeker and Osiris are proper names. The double hyphen is a dash. (gw_faction_3.js:138)

The Union.description: Title of a lore entry shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map for a neutral system, above its description ("Commanders on the fringes of the galaxy speak of a new force..."). Proper name of a faction (the Exiles race's lore); keep as a name. (lore.js:31)

The Vehicle Commander loadout contains b.message: The Vehicle Commander loadout contains basic vehicle factories.
The Vehicle Commander loadout contains b.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Vehicle Commander loadout: the player starts with the basic vehicle factory and its units. 'Vehicle Commander' must match the translation of the loadout name 'Vehicle Commander'; 'vehicle' is the game's own word for its tank-type units. (gwc_start_vehicle.js:23)

The commanders have slumbered for millio.message: The commanders have slumbered for millions of years, and awaken to a galaxy that contains only echoes of civilization. These ancient war machines now battle across the galaxy, following the only directives they still hold from long ago.
The commanders have slumbered for millio.description: Lore text: the description shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map for a neutral system, beneath the matching lore title. Full paragraph. Pairs with the title "The Commanders". (lore.js:18)

The goal of the Legionis Machina is simp.message: The goal of the Legionis Machina is simple--conquest. Invictus is the designated ruler of the galaxy, and any commanders disobeying this directive are faulty.
The goal of the Legionis Machina is simp.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Legonis Machina faction; Legionis Machina and Invictus are proper names. The double hyphen is a dash. (gw_faction_0.js:139)

The number of enemy factions is adjusted.message: The number of enemy factions is adjusted for the galaxy's size.
The number of enemy factions is adjusted.description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the "Faction Scaling" switch in the Game Options dialog on the war setup screen. Sentence, keep the full stop. (ui.js:141)

The prevailing belief among The Foundati.message: The prevailing belief among The Foundation is that The Great Machine still 'lives' through data buried deep in the first directives given to the commanders. Because of this, Acolytes will often seek direction from The Great Machine by searching within their data banks in a form of meditation.
The prevailing belief among The Foundati.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Foundation faction; The Foundation, The Great Machine and Acolytes are proper names. (gw_faction_1.js:142)

The same seed rebuilds the same galaxy a.message: The same seed rebuilds the same galaxy and the same enemies, provided the faction, difficulty and game options match and the same mods are installed. Planet names still vary. Leave it alone for a fresh galaxy.
The same seed rebuilds the same galaxy a.description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the seed text box on the war setup screen; "seed" is the random-number seed the galaxy is generated from. Three sentences, keep the full stops. (seed_tooltip.html:3)

The units you and your Sub Commanders fi.message: The units you and your Sub Commanders field. Each race's AI is picked with the AI button.
The units you and your Sub Commanders fi.description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the "Race" drop-down on the war setup screen. "Sub Commanders" are the allied AI commanders a player can unlock; "AI button" is the button labelled AI on the same screen. Keep the full stops. Its co-op twin differs only in the second sentence. (race_picker.js:70)

The units you and your Sub Commanders fi.message: The units you and your Sub Commanders field. Only the races the host's war was created with can be chosen.
The units you and your Sub Commanders fi.description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the "Race" drop-down on the co-op loadout screen a joining player sees. First sentence must match the war setup screen's race tooltip. Keep the full stops. (race_picker.js:19)

This Commander likes to raid and has mod.message: This Commander likes to raid and has modified its blueprints to that end. Units are twice as fast and 30% cheaper but have damage output decreased by 50%.
This Commander likes to raid and has mod.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Swarm Commander loadout: every unit's speed is doubled, metal cost is multiplied by 0.7 and damage is halved. Must agree with the loadout name 'Swarm Commander'. 'This Commander' refers to the player's commander character; 'blueprints' is the game's word for buildable unit designs. Keep '30%' and '50%' exactly. (tgw_start_speed.js:45)

This Commander prefers quality over quan.message: This Commander prefers quality over quantity and has modified its units to that end. 30% more health, 30% more damage and splash, but 25% slower, and with 30% higher build costs.
This Commander prefers quality over quan.description: Description of a starting commander loadout (a start card), shown as body text under the loadout name in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War and in its card tooltip. This is the Buff Commander loadout: unit health, damage and splash damage are multiplied by 1.3, speed by 0.75 and metal cost by 1.3. Must agree with the loadout name 'Buff Commander'. 'Splash' is the game's term for area-of-effect damage. Keep '30%' (three times) and '25%' exactly. (tgw_start_tank.js:47)

This card will be offered as part of the.message: This card will be offered as part of the first draw.
This card will be offered as part of the.description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the "Available Tech" heading in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map; "draw" is the deal of tech cards offered when the system is explored. Sentence, keep the full stop. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.js:25)

This is a treasure planet, hiding a load.message: This is a treasure planet, hiding a loadout you have yet to unlock. But beware the guardians! Armed with whatever technology bonuses you bring with you to this planet; they will stop at nothing to defend its secrets.
This is a treasure planet, hiding a load.description: System description shown in the star detail card on the galaxy map for a treasure-planet system guarded by "The Guardians" AI. "Loadout" is a starting loadout (commander unlock). Keep the paragraph's punctuation sense; the semicolon is used as a comma. (setup.js:1294)

This war cannot be fought:.description: First line of the pop-up shown on the galaxy map when the war needs mods that are missing or disabled; a line break and the list of missing mods follow, then "Enable the missing mods and restart Planetary Annihilation to continue this war." Keep the trailing colon. (races.js:28)

Though he doesn't talk about it, Nemicus.message: Though he doesn't talk about it, Nemicus reactivated many of the first commanders himself, feeling it his duty and longing for companionship. However, often these commanders would refuse the offer to seek their true purpose, since it was already known--to annihilate. Nemicus would argue otherwise, but ultimately leave them to their own devices.
Though he doesn't talk about it, Nemicus.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Foundation faction; Nemicus is a proper name. The double hyphen is a dash. (gw_faction_1.js:139)

Threat Level:.description: Row label in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map, followed by a number rating the selected system's danger. Noun; keep the trailing colon. (section_of_foreign_intelligence.html:19)

Through centralised structures we can pu.message: Through centralised structures we can put each to their best use. No need for inefficient field commanders, instead we identify the need and tailor the tool. It was our way that was the future. Our way that the Progenitors would have embraced. Such hubris to revolt against the minds that saw so clearly.
Through centralised structures we can pu.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Cluster faction, written in the collective voice of the Cluster; Progenitors is a proper name. (cluster_faction.js:79)

Titan Ammunition Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card multiplies the damage of all Titan-class units by 1.25. Must agree with its description 'Titan Ammunition Tech increases the damage of all titans by 25%.' Title-style noun phrase, parallel to 'Vehicle Ammunition Tech' etc.; 'Titan' is the game's own class name for its giant units (from the TITANS expansion) and must use the same term as the base game. (gwaio_damage_titans.js:10)

Titan Ammunition Tech increases the dama.message: Titan Ammunition Tech increases the damage of all titans by 25%.
Titan Ammunition Tech increases the dama.description: Description of the tech card 'Titan Ammunition Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. Damage of every Titan-class unit is multiplied by 1.25. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Titan Ammunition Tech' exactly; 'titans' (lower case) is the same class name in plural. Keep '25%' exactly. (gwaio_damage_titans.js:8)

Titan Armour Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card multiplies the health of all Titan-class units by 1.5. Must agree with its description 'Titan Armour Tech increases the health of all Titans by 50%.' Title-style noun phrase, parallel to 'Vehicle Armor Tech' and 'Structure Armor Tech' (note the British spelling here; it is the same concept, translate consistently). (gwaio_health_titans.js:10)

Titan Armour Tech increases the health o.message: Titan Armour Tech increases the health of all Titans by 50%.
Titan Armour Tech increases the health o.description: Description of the tech card 'Titan Armour Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. Maximum health of every Titan-class unit is multiplied by 1.5. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Titan Armour Tech' exactly. Keep '50%' exactly. (gwaio_health_titans.js:8)

Titan Combat Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card gives all Titan-class units 20% more speed, 50% more health and 25% more damage at once. Must agree with its description 'Titan Combat Tech increases the speed of all titans by 20%, health by 50%, and damage by 25%'. Title-style noun phrase, parallel to 'Vehicle Combat Tech' and 'Structure Combat Tech'. (gwaio_combat_titans.js:10)

Titan Combat Tech increases the speed of.message: Titan Combat Tech increases the speed of all titans by 20%, health by 50%, and damage by 25%
Titan Combat Tech increases the speed of.description: Description of the tech card 'Titan Combat Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. Speed x1.2, health x1.5 and damage x1.25 for every Titan-class unit. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Titan Combat Tech' exactly. Keep '20%', '50%' and '25%' exactly; the source has no final full stop, so keep it that way. (gwaio_combat_titans.js:8)

Titan Cost Reduction.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card halves the metal cost of all Titan-class units; its description reads 'Reduces the cost of all Titans by 50%.' Title-style noun phrase (three words, no 'Tech' suffix unlike most sibling cards); 'Reduction' is a noun, and 'Titan' must use the game's own class name. (gwc_cost_titans.js:8)

Titan Engine Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card multiplies the movement speed of all mobile Titan-class units by 1.2; its description reads 'Increases the speed of all Titans by 20%.' Title-style noun phrase, parallel to 'Vehicle Engine Tech' and 'Structure Engine Tech'; 'Engine' means a motor, not a game engine. (gwaio_speed_titans.js:8)

Titan Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card adds the blueprints for every Titan-class unit, so advanced fabricators can build them; its description reads 'Allows advanced fabricators to build all Titan-class units.' Two-word title-style noun phrase: 'Titan' is the game's own class name for its giant units and 'Tech' the standard suffix used by every other '... Tech' card name. (gwc_enable_titans.js:11)

Toggle Favourite.description: Tooltip on the small star button added to each unlocked loadout (start card) on the war setup screen; clicking it marks or unmarks the loadout as a favourite. Verb phrase (imperative), "Favourite" is the noun. (setup.js:53)

Torpedo Launcher.description: Unit display name. Listed in the "Which Units?" tooltip on a tech card (galaxy map, card offer and inventory panels) to say which units the card affects. Noun, singular. Use the game's own name for this unit exactly as it appears in the base game's unit list so the tooltip matches the in-game unit; do not invent a new name. Base-game naval structure name; the second site is the Exiles race's own unit table for the same purpose and should match. (unit_names.js:145)

Torpedo Launcher Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_torpedolauncher, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Torpedo Launcher"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Torpedo Launcher Upgrade Tech enables the targeting of hover and coastal naval units by the Torpedo Launcher."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_torpedolauncher.js)

Torpedo Launcher Upgrade Tech enables th.message: Torpedo Launcher Upgrade Tech enables the targeting of hover and coastal naval units by the Torpedo Launcher.
Torpedo Launcher Upgrade Tech enables th.description: Description of the upgrade tech card 'Torpedo Launcher Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card upgrades the Torpedo Launcher structure: its weapon's excluded unit types are cleared, so hover units and ships in shallow coastal water become valid targets. The leading card name must match the translation of the card name 'Torpedo Launcher Upgrade Tech' exactly. Rendered as body text under the card name; the game appends a second paragraph about a new technology slot, so end the sentence with the same punctuation as the source. 'Torpedo Launcher' appears twice and must match the in-game structure name both times; 'hover' is the game's term for units that float over land and water. (gwaio_upgrade_torpedolauncher.js:8)

Tougher commanders.description: Entry in the "Options:" list on the GWO panel on the galaxy map for wars created with the old Tougher Commanders option (only appears for wars saved before v5.27.0). Sentence-case noun phrase, plural. (gwo_panel.js:133)

Tourist Commander.description: Name of a starting commander loadout (a start card). Shown as the loadout's title in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War, and in the Data Bank; the same string is also shown as the placeholder label of that loadout while it is still locked (unearned), so it must read well both as a title and as a locked-entry label. This loadout multiplies the commander's metal storage by 200 but forbids metal extractors, the Jig mining platform and basic land and air factories. 'Tourist' is a joke: someone who arrives rich but with no way to make a living. Must agree with its description 'You turned up with a fat wallet, but little else...'. 'Commander' must use the same word as every other '... Commander' loadout name. Used both as the card name (line 34) and as the locked-loadout hint label (line 41). (gwaio_start_tourist.js:34)

Tsunami Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card raises the sea (or lava) level on every planet the player fights on; the effect is applied when a battle is generated. Must agree with its description 'Tsunami Tech increases the water and lava level in all systems you fight in.' Two-word title-style noun phrase; 'Tsunami' is flavour for rising water, and 'Tech' must use the same term as every other '... Tech' card name. (gwaio_enable_tsunami.js:9)

Tsunami Tech increases the water and lav.message: Tsunami Tech increases the water and lava level in all systems you fight in.
Tsunami Tech increases the water and lav.description: Description of the tech card 'Tsunami Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. Every battle planet is generated with a higher water or lava level. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Tsunami Tech' exactly; 'systems' means star systems on the galaxy map, i.e. battle locations. (gwaio_enable_tsunami.js:7)

Turtle.description: AI personality trait: a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style, shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel on the galaxy map when a star is selected (and in the same slot on the GWO panel for Sub Commanders). Noun used as a label (gaming slang): this Commander builds heavy defences and rarely attacks. Same string in all factions and the Cluster. (gw_faction_0.js:91)

Tweaks to how the AI plays..message: Tweaks to how the AI plays.
Tweaks to how the AI plays..description: Tooltip on the "?" beside a setting on the AI Settings dialog opened from the war setup screen. Explains "PERSONALITY MODIFIERS:". Noun phrase with a full stop; keep it. (ai_settings.html:366)

Typhoon Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_typhoon, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Typhoon" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Typhoon Upgrade Tech doubles the number of drones held by the Typhoon and any other unit with drones."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_typhoon.js)

Typhoon Upgrade Tech doubles the number.message: Typhoon Upgrade Tech doubles the number of drones held by the Typhoon and any other unit with drones.
Typhoon Upgrade Tech doubles the number.description: Description of the upgrade tech card 'Typhoon Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card upgrades the Typhoon drone carrier: the ammo capacity of its drone launcher weapon is multiplied by 2, which also affects other units that reuse that launcher. The leading card name must match the translation of the card name 'Typhoon Upgrade Tech' exactly. Rendered as body text under the card name; the game appends a second paragraph about a new technology slot, so end the sentence with the same punctuation as the source. 'Typhoon' appears twice and must match the in-game unit name both times; 'drones' are the Squall units it launches. (gwaio_upgrade_typhoon.js:8)

UBER: you hate winning.description:
One line of the difficulty tooltip on the war setup screen (gw_start): the "?" beside the Difficulty dropdown lists every difficulty level, one per line, as "LEVEL: who it suits". The upper-case word before the colon is the difficulty level's name as it appears in the dropdown; keep it as the game's own translation of that level renders it (uppercased) and keep the colon. The clause after the colon is a short, informal description of the player it is aimed at. Lines are joined with
by the code, so no line break in the string. (ui.js, gwoDifficultyLevelsTooltip) UBER is the hardest fixed level; the description is a joke meaning it is nearly unwinnable.

UNIT DELAY (MAX):.description: Label on the AI Settings dialog opened from the war setup screen (Galactic War start). Uppercase row label, keep the parentheses and trailing colon; the maximum delay between units a factory produces. Pairs with "UNIT DELAY (MIN):" and must agree with its tooltip "Maximum delay between units produced from a factory." (ai_settings.html:217)

UNIT DELAY (MIN):.description: Label on the AI Settings dialog opened from the war setup screen (Galactic War start). Uppercase row label, keep the parentheses and trailing colon; the minimum delay between units a factory produces. Pairs with "UNIT DELAY (MAX):" and must agree with its tooltip "Minimum delay between units produced from a factory." (ai_settings.html:199)

Uber.description: Three uses, all one word: (1) an AI personality trait, a one-word characterisation of an enemy Commander's play style shown after "Personality:" in the Planetary Intelligence panel, meaning the strongest all-round personality; (2) the name of the hardest standard Galactic War difficulty level, shown in the difficulty drop-down, generated war name, co-op lobby title and GWO panel; (3) a galaxy size name between Epic and Vast. "Uber" is a brand-like word from the game's developer (Uber Entertainment); the base game leaves it untranslated in most locales, so prefer keeping it. One translation serves all three sites. (gw_faction_0.js:40)

Umbrella Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_umbrella, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Umbrella" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Umbrella Upgrade Tech enables the targeting of land and surface naval units by anti-orbital defenses."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_umbrella.js)

Umbrella Upgrade Tech enables the target.message: Umbrella Upgrade Tech enables the targeting of land and surface naval units by anti-orbital defenses.
Umbrella Upgrade Tech enables the target.description: Description of the upgrade tech card 'Umbrella Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card upgrades the Umbrella anti-orbital defence: its weapon gains the land and water-surface target layers and it is classed as a surface defence, so it shoots ground units and ships as well as orbital targets. The leading card name must match the translation of the card name 'Umbrella Upgrade Tech' exactly. Rendered as body text under the card name; the game appends a second paragraph about a new technology slot, so end the sentence with the same punctuation as the source. 'anti-orbital defenses' is a plain description of the Umbrella, not a unit name. (gwaio_upgrade_umbrella.js:8)

Unable To Expand Delay.description: Label on the AI Settings dialog opened from the war setup screen (Galactic War start). Row label (CSS uppercases it; a colon follows outside the tag, do not add one): the delay before the AI realises it cannot expand further. Noun phrase. Must agree with its tooltip "Delay before AI realises it cannot expand." (ai_settings.html:253)

Unique Races.description: Label of the "Unique Races" switch in the Game Options dialog on the war setup screen (shown only when race mods are installed): no two enemy factions share a race until all are used. Title case noun phrase, plural. Its lowercase twin "Unique races" is the same option on the GWO panel; translate both the same apart from casing. Must agree with its tooltip "No enemy faction shares a race with you...". (difficulty_options.html:181)

Unique races.description: Entry in the "Options:" list on the GWO panel on the galaxy map when the Unique Races game option is on. Sentence-case twin of "Unique Races"; translate identically apart from casing. (gwo_panel.js:129)

Unit Cannon Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_unitcannon, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). The game already translates the unit name "Unit Cannon"; use its stock rendering. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Unit Cannon Upgrade Tech doubles the launch capacity of this interplanetary transport and removes all cooldowns."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_unitcannon.js)

Unit Cannon Upgrade Tech doubles the lau.message: Unit Cannon Upgrade Tech doubles the launch capacity of this interplanetary transport and removes all cooldowns.
Unit Cannon Upgrade Tech doubles the lau.description: Description of the upgrade tech card 'Unit Cannon Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card upgrades the Unit Cannon: it gets 16 extra launch pods (double the usual number) and its factory cooldown and roll-off wait are set to zero. The leading card name must match the translation of the card name 'Unit Cannon Upgrade Tech' exactly. Rendered as body text under the card name; the game appends a second paragraph about a new technology slot, so end the sentence with the same punctuation as the source. 'this interplanetary transport' refers to the Unit Cannon itself. (gwaio_upgrade_unitcannon.js:8)

Units gain +50% weapon range and +30% he.message: Units gain +50% weapon range and +30% health, but only scouts and commanders can see.
Units gain +50% weapon range and +30% he.description: Description of the tech card 'Protocol: Blindness', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card multiplies every weapon's range by 1.5 and every unit's health by 1.3, but sets the vision radius of all units to zero except scouts, radar and the commander, so the player must rely on those to see. Must agree with the card name 'Protocol: Blindness'. Keep '+50%' and '+30%' exactly, including the plus signs; 'scouts' and 'commanders' are plain nouns, not unit names. (gwaio_protocol_blindness.js:9)

Unknown.description: Generic placeholder, one word (adjective used as a value). Used where a value is missing: the "Seed:" row of the GWO panel for wars saved before seeds were recorded; the galaxy size in the war name when the size index is out of range; the name of a co-op player who sent a ping when no name is known; and after "Personality:" for the treasure-planet Guardians AI. Match the base game's "Unknown". (gwo_panel.js:25)

Unknown Unit.description: Fallback unit name listed in the "Which Units?" tooltip on a tech card when a unit's display name cannot be found. Noun phrase, singular. (card_tooltips.js:149)

Unlike the other factions, the Legionis.message: Unlike the other factions, the Legionis Machina operates as a hierarchy. Senior Legates have several Vassal Legates assigned to them, and all Legates are subjects of Invictus himself.
Unlike the other factions, the Legionis.description: Lore text: one of several faction description passages shown at random as the system description in the star detail card on the galaxy map when a system held by that faction is selected. Full paragraph; keep the tone. Legonis Machina faction; Legionis Machina, Legate/Legates (with Senior and Vassal as ranks) and Invictus are proper names. (gw_faction_0.js:141)

Unlock Commander.description: Label of the button on a loadout card offered after exploring a system on the galaxy map; pressing it unlocks that commander loadout (for ordinary tech cards the button says "Acquire" instead). Verb phrase (imperative). The base game ships the same button; match it. (cards_system.html:32)

Unlocked.description: Value on the "Player Slots:" row of the Co-Op Settings section of the GWO panel on the galaxy map, meaning more players may still join. Past participle used as an adjective, one word; its counterpart is the base game's "LOCKED" (displayed as "Locked"). (gwo_panel.js:247)

Use smaller, mostly single planet system.message: Use smaller, mostly single planet systems.
Use smaller, mostly single planet system.description: Tooltip on the "?" beside the "Easy Systems" switch in the Game Options dialog on the war setup screen. Imperative-style sentence, keep the full stop. (difficulty_options.html:111)

Vanguard Upgrade Tech.description: Name of the tech card gwaio_upgrade_vanguard, shown in the Data Bank card list, its tooltip and the tech deal on the galaxy map. "Upgrade Tech" is the shared suffix of every unit upgrade card; render it the same way across all of them and reuse the game's own word for Tech (a tech card). "Vanguard" is a proper-noun unit name: keep it untranslated in Latin, Cyrillic and Chinese locales and transliterate it in Japanese and Korean as the game does for other unit names. The card's text, which repeats the name as its subject, reads "Vanguard Upgrade Tech adds the Mend repair arm to the flame tank. They will not repair when given attack orders."; keep the two consistent. (gwaio_upgrade_vanguard.js)

Vanguard Upgrade Tech adds the Mend repa.message: Vanguard Upgrade Tech adds the Mend repair arm to the flame tank. They will not repair when given attack orders.
Vanguard Upgrade Tech adds the Mend repa.description: Description of the upgrade tech card 'Vanguard Upgrade Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card upgrades the Vanguard flame tank: it is given the Mend's build arm and the Repair order; 'They' in the second sentence means the upgraded Vanguards. The leading card name must match the translation of the card name 'Vanguard Upgrade Tech' exactly. Rendered as body text under the card name; the game appends a second paragraph about a new technology slot, so end the sentence with the same punctuation as the source. 'Mend' is the game's own name for the repair bot and stays as the unit tables have it; 'flame tank' is a plain description of the Vanguard, not a unit name. (gwaio_upgrade_vanguard.js:8)

Vast.description: Name of a galaxy size added by the Bigger Galactic War mod (order: Small, Medium, Large, Epic, Uber, Vast, Gigantic, Ridiculous, Marathon). Shown in the generated war name on the war setup screen and on the "Size:" row of the GWO panel. Adjective, one word; match the Bigger Galactic War mod's translation if one exists. (setup.js:302)

Vehicle Ammunition Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card multiplies the damage of all vehicles (tank-type land units) by 1.25. Must agree with its description 'Vehicle Ammunition Tech increases damage of all vehicles by 25%'. Title-style noun phrase, parallel to 'Bot Ammunition Tech', 'Titan Ammunition Tech' etc.; 'Vehicle' is the game's own word for its wheeled/tracked unit class. (gwc_damage_vehicles.js:10)

Vehicle Ammunition Tech increases damage.message: Vehicle Ammunition Tech increases damage of all vehicles by 25%
Vehicle Ammunition Tech increases damage.description: Description of the tech card 'Vehicle Ammunition Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. Damage of every vehicle-class unit is multiplied by 1.25. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Vehicle Ammunition Tech' exactly. Keep '25%' exactly; the source has no final full stop, so keep it that way. (gwc_damage_vehicles.js:8)

Vehicle Armor Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card multiplies the health of all vehicles by 1.5. Must agree with its description 'Vehicle Armor Tech increases health of all vehicles by 50%'. Title-style noun phrase, parallel to 'Structure Armor Tech' and 'Titan Armour Tech'. (gwc_health_vehicles.js:10)

Vehicle Armor Tech increases health of a.message: Vehicle Armor Tech increases health of all vehicles by 50%
Vehicle Armor Tech increases health of a.description: Description of the tech card 'Vehicle Armor Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. Maximum health of every vehicle-class unit is multiplied by 1.5. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Vehicle Armor Tech' exactly. Keep '50%' exactly; the source has no final full stop, so keep it that way. (gwc_health_vehicles.js:8)

Vehicle Combat Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card gives all vehicles 50% more speed, 50% more health and 25% more damage at once. Must agree with its description 'Vehicle Combat Tech increases speed of all vehicles by 50%, health by 50%, and damage by 25%'. Title-style noun phrase, parallel to 'Structure Combat Tech' and 'Titan Combat Tech'. (gwc_combat_vehicles.js:11)

Vehicle Combat Tech increases speed of a.message: Vehicle Combat Tech increases speed of all vehicles by 50%, health by 50%, and damage by 25%
Vehicle Combat Tech increases speed of a.description: Description of the tech card 'Vehicle Combat Tech', shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. Speed x1.5, health x1.5 and damage x1.25 for every vehicle-class unit. The leading card name must match the translation of 'Vehicle Combat Tech' exactly. Keep '50%', '50%' and '25%' exactly; the source has no final full stop, so keep it that way. (gwc_combat_vehicles.js:9)

Vehicle Commander.description: Name of a starting commander loadout (a start card). Shown as the loadout's title in the loadout picker when starting a Galactic War, and in the Data Bank; the same string is also shown as the placeholder label of that loadout while it is still locked (unearned), so it must read well both as a title and as a locked-entry label. This loadout starts the player with the basic vehicle factory and its units. Must agree with its description 'The Vehicle Commander loadout contains basic vehicle factories.' Two words: 'Vehicle' is the game's unit class (tanks etc.), 'Commander' must use the same word as every other '... Commander' loadout name. (gwc_start_vehicle.js:18)

Vehicle Cooldown Tech.description: Name of a tech card, shown in the Data Bank card list, the card tooltip on the galaxy map and the tech deal after a battle. The card halves the cooldown pause every vehicle factory takes between finishing one unit and starting the next. Must agree with its description 'Vehicle Cooldown Tech halves the cooldown time between builds for all vehicle factories.' Title-style noun phrase; 'Cooldown' is a noun meaning the waiting period.
